title: ZOLL AED 3 Defibrillator - ECG Analysis Will Not Start or Complete
description: Troubleshooting delayed, interrupted, or incomplete rhythm analysis caused by electrode pads, patient contact, movement, connections, battery condition, or device readiness.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting while the ZOLL AED 3 is the only defibrillator available for a patient in suspected cardiac arrest. If ECG analysis will not begin or complete during a rescue: Continue CPR according to the responding clinical team’s protocol. Obtain another verified AED or manual defibrillator immediately. Do not delay resuscitation while attempting repeated equipment tests. Follow the facility’s emergency equipment-failure procedure. Ensure no one is touching or moving the patient when an AED is actively attempting rhythm analysis. Expected outcome: Resuscitation continues without depending on a device whose rhythm-analysis function is uncertain. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the AED has been removed from active patient use.

steps.title: 2. Record the Exact Failure Behavior
steps.instructions: Power on the AED and document what occurs after the pads are connected. Determine whether: Analysis never begins. The device repeatedly instructs the responder to attach the pads. Analysis begins but is interrupted. A “Do Not Touch Patient” instruction is given but no decision follows. The device returns to CPR prompts without completing analysis. A pad, battery, readiness, or service message appears. The display freezes or the voice prompts stop. Expected outcome: The failure is separated into a pad-detection, signal-quality, power, control, or internal-device problem.

steps.title: 3. Check the Readiness Indicator
steps.instructions: Turn the AED off and inspect its readiness indicator. Confirm that: The green check mark is displayed. No red “X” or other failed-readiness indication is present. The AED does not emit periodic warning beeps. No service or maintenance message appears when the unit is powered on. A failed readiness indicator suggests that the AED has detected a condition affecting its ability to remain rescue ready. ZOLL recommends routine checks of the readiness indicator, battery, pads, and device condition. Expected outcome: The AED shows a normal readiness condition. If the readiness check fails, remove the AED from service and evaluate the reported fault before continuing.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Electrode-Pad Package
steps.instructions: Verify that the installed electrodes are approved for the ZOLL AED 3 and are within their expiration date. Inspect for: Opened, torn, punctured, or unsealed packaging. Moisture intrusion. Dried or damaged conductive gel. Bent, contaminated, or damaged connector contacts. Crushed or sharply folded pad cables. Evidence that the pads were previously used. Incorrect or incompatible electrode pads. Expected outcome: The pads are compatible, sealed, undamaged, and unexpired. Replace questionable pads with a new verified set. If analysis then operates normally, stop and return the AED to service after completing the required functional and readiness checks.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Pad Connector
steps.instructions: Confirm that the electrode connector is fully inserted into the AED. Disconnect and reconnect the plug while inspecting for: Partial insertion. Debris or contamination. Bent or recessed contacts. Cracked connector housing. Loose fit. Damaged cable strain relief. Damage to the AED connector receptacle. Do not insert tools into the connector or attempt to straighten internal contacts while the AED is powered. Expected outcome: The connector seats securely and the AED recognizes that pads are attached. If reconnecting the pads restores normal detection and analysis, stop and document the connection issue.

steps.title: 6. Confirm Correct Pad Application During a Controlled Test
steps.instructions: Use an approved defibrillator analyzer or manufacturer-compatible test load. Do not test analysis or shock functions on a person. Confirm that: Both electrodes are connected to the analyzer as required. The entire conductive surface is making contact. The pad cable is not under tension. No insulating material is between the pads and analyzer contacts. The analyzer is configured to produce an AED-recognizable ECG rhythm. The AED must receive an adequate ECG signal through the therapy electrodes before it can classify the rhythm. ZOLL specifies an analysis function that evaluates the ECG and advises or delivers a shock when a shockable rhythm is detected. Expected outcome: The AED detects the connected electrodes and begins rhythm analysis.

steps.title: 7. Eliminate Motion and Electrical Interference
steps.instructions: During analysis testing: Stop movement of the analyzer, pads, and cables. Do not handle the pads or connector. Keep the AED away from operating electrosurgical equipment. Move mobile transmitters and other possible interference sources away from the setup. Confirm that the analyzer signal is stable. Remove unnecessary accessories or cables near the test area. Patient movement, CPR activity, poor electrode contact, or electrical noise can produce artifact that prevents reliable rhythm classification. Expected outcome: Analysis proceeds without repeated interruption or prolonged delay. If eliminating motion or interference resolves the issue, repeat the test to confirm consistent operation.

steps.title: 8. Substitute a Verified Set of Pads
steps.instructions: Connect a new, unexpired set of compatible ZOLL AED 3 electrodes to the analyzer. Repeat the analysis test using the same analyzer rhythm and setup. Expected outcome: If the AED analyzes normally, the original pads or pad cable were defective. If the failure remains, continue troubleshooting the AED and test equipment. Do not return opened troubleshooting pads to emergency deployment unless permitted by facility policy and their integrity remains fully acceptable.

steps.title: 9. Verify the Defibrillator Analyzer
steps.instructions: Confirm that the analyzer: Passes its own operational checks. Produces a stable ECG waveform. Is configured for the intended rhythm. Has compatible and secure adapter connections. Successfully initiates AED analysis on another verified defibrillator, when available. A weak, unstable, or incompatible analyzer signal can imitate an AED analysis failure. Expected outcome: The analyzer and adapters are verified independently. If another AED also fails to analyze the same test setup, correct the analyzer, adapter, or simulation configuration before condemning the ZOLL AED 3.

steps.title: 10. Check Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect the AED battery for: Low-battery messages. Expiration or replacement-date concerns. Cracked housing. Contaminated contacts. Improper seating. Corrosion or moisture. Evidence of swelling, leakage, or overheating. Reseat the battery if permitted by facility procedure, then power on the AED and observe the startup behavior. Expected outcome: The AED starts normally without battery or readiness warnings and remains powered throughout testing. Replace a questionable battery with a verified compatible battery. If analysis then completes normally, perform the required readiness and functional checks before returning the AED to service.

steps.title: 11. Restart the AED
steps.instructions: Turn the AED off, wait briefly, and power it on again with the verified battery and pads connected. Observe whether: Startup completes normally. Voice and visual prompts remain synchronized. Pad recognition occurs. Analysis begins. A rhythm decision is reached. The AED unexpectedly restarts, freezes, or loses audio. Expected outcome: A complete uninterrupted analysis cycle occurs. A restart that temporarily clears the problem does not establish reliable operation. Repeat the test several times before considering the device functional.

steps.title: 12. Test Shockable and Non-Shockable Rhythms
steps.instructions: Using the approved analyzer, test at least: One shockable rhythm. One non-shockable rhythm. Confirm that the AED: Recognizes the connected pads. Announces that analysis is occurring. Completes analysis within a reasonable period. Provides the appropriate shock or no-shock decision. Does not repeatedly interrupt or restart analysis. Provides normal display and voice instructions. The AED 3 uses ZOLL’s RapidShock analysis system and is designed to reach a treatment decision quickly after compressions stop. Expected outcome: Analysis completes consistently for both rhythm categories and the displayed decision agrees with the analyzer setting. Do not deliver an unnecessary test shock unless required by the approved inspection procedure and the analyzer is rated to receive it.

steps.title: 13. Inspect the AED Externally
steps.instructions: Examine the unit for: Impact or drop damage. Cracks near the pad connector. Liquid intrusion. Loose housing sections. Damaged battery compartment. Unresponsive touchscreen controls. Distorted or missing audio. Unusual heat, odor, or sounds. Evidence of unauthorized repair. Expected outcome: No external condition is found that could compromise ECG acquisition or safe defibrillator operation. Do not open the enclosure or proceed with internal board-level troubleshooting unless authorized, trained, and working from the current ZOLL service documentation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the ZOLL AED 3 recognized the pads but repeatedly failed to complete ECG rhythm analysis.
CCR.Cause: Testing found an intermittent connection in the expired CPR Uni-padz cable that caused repeated pad-detection and analysis interruptions.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the electrode pads, verified the green readiness indicator, and successfully completed repeated shockable and non-shockable rhythm-analysis tests using a defibrillator analyzer.

helpfulDetails: Whether analysis started or was interrupted
Any freezes, restarts, or audio failures
Unusual heat, smell, sounds, or physical damage

title: ZOLL AED 3 Defibrillator - Shock Button Not Responding
description: Troubleshooting a shock button that does not illuminate, activate, or deliver an advised shock due to operating state, pads, power, contamination, or damage.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting while the ZOLL AED 3 is the only defibrillator available for a patient in cardiac arrest. If the shock button does not respond during a rescue: Continue high-quality CPR. Notify the responding clinical team immediately. Obtain another verified AED or defibrillator without delay. Follow the device’s voice and visual prompts while the replacement is being prepared. Do not repeatedly press an unresponsive button or delay resuscitation efforts. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without depending on a defibrillator with uncertain shock-delivery capability. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the AED has been removed from active patient use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the AED Configuration
steps.instructions: Verify whether the device is a semiautomatic ZOLL AED 3 with a shock button or a fully automatic configuration. A fully automatic AED delivers an advised shock without requiring the rescuer to press a shock button. A semiautomatic AED instructs the rescuer to press the button after detecting a shockable rhythm. Expected outcome: The reported behavior matches the AED’s intended configuration. If the unit is fully automatic, the absence of manual shock-button operation is normal. Stop troubleshooting and correct any misunderstanding regarding device operation.

steps.title: 3. Confirm That a Shock Was Actually Advised
steps.instructions: Review the reported event and determine whether the AED: Completed rhythm analysis. Announced or displayed that a shock was advised. Charged for shock delivery. Illuminated or otherwise activated the shock button. Instructed the rescuer to press the shock button. The shock button is not expected to deliver energy unless the AED has analyzed the rhythm, identified a shockable condition, and completed charging. Expected outcome: The AED reaches the shock-ready state before button operation is evaluated. If no shock was advised, the inactive shock button may represent normal operation rather than a failure.

steps.title: 4. Check the Readiness Indicator
steps.instructions: With the AED out of service, inspect its readiness indicator and record its condition. Look for: A normal ready indication. A failed or not-ready indication. Audible warning tones. Displayed fault messages. Evidence that the device recently failed a self-test. ZOLL recommends checking the AED readiness status and inspecting the battery, electrode pads, and device condition as part of routine readiness verification. Expected outcome: The AED indicates that it is ready for use without an active fault. If the readiness indicator shows a failure, remove the AED from service and address the reported fault before attempting further functional verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Shock Button Externally
steps.instructions: Visually inspect the shock button and surrounding housing for: Cracks or impact damage. A button stuck below the bezel. Debris around the button edge. Dried fluids or cleaning residue. Warped or separated housing. An abnormal or absent tactile response. Do not insert tools around the button or apply excessive force. Expected outcome: The shock button moves normally and shows no external damage or obstruction. If the button is physically damaged, stuck, or contaminated internally, stop testing and send the AED for repair.

steps.title: 6. Clean External Contamination Safely
steps.instructions: Power down the AED and clean the button area using only facility-approved methods and products compatible with the manufacturer’s cleaning requirements. Do not spray fluid directly onto the AED. Do not allow liquid to enter the button opening or enclosure. Do not use sharp objects to remove debris. Allow the device to dry completely before retesting. Expected outcome: External residue is removed and normal button movement is restored. If cleaning restores normal operation, complete the required functional verification before returning the AED to service.

steps.title: 7. Check the Battery Installation
steps.instructions: Remove and reinstall the battery according to the approved facility procedure. Inspect for: A battery that is not fully seated. Cracked or damaged battery housing. Contaminated or damaged accessible contacts. An expired or depleted battery. A battery-related message or readiness failure. Use a known-good, compatible battery when available. Expected outcome: The AED powers on normally, completes its startup checks, and displays no battery-related fault. If a known-good battery resolves the issue, replace the defective battery and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 8. Inspect the Electrode Pads and Connection
steps.instructions: Confirm that the installed electrode pads: Are approved for the ZOLL AED 3. Are within their expiration date. Have unopened, undamaged packaging. Have an intact cable and connector. Are fully connected to the AED as required. Match the intended adult or pediatric application. An incomplete pad connection or pad-related fault can prevent normal rhythm analysis and keep the AED from reaching the shock-ready state. Expected outcome: The AED recognizes the connected pads and does not display a pad or connection warning. If replacing the pad set resolves the condition, document the failed accessory and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 9. Review Event Data and Reported Prompts
steps.instructions: When event data are available, review the rescue record or device logs to determine: Whether a shockable rhythm was identified. Whether charging completed. Whether the shock button was activated. Whether the button press was recorded. Whether the charge timed out. Whether a device, battery, or pad fault occurred. Also interview the reporting staff to determine whether the button: Never illuminated. Illuminated but did not respond. Required multiple presses. Delivered the shock after a delay. Became inactive before it was pressed. Expected outcome: The sequence identifies whether the problem occurred during analysis, charging, button activation, or shock delivery.

steps.title: 10. Perform an Approved Functional Test
steps.instructions: Move the AED to a controlled bench-testing area and connect it to an approved AED analyzer or simulator. Using the facility’s approved inspection procedure: Confirm normal startup and readiness status. Simulate a shockable rhythm. Verify that the AED analyzes the rhythm. Confirm that a shock is advised. Verify that the AED charges normally. Confirm that the shock button illuminates or becomes active. Press the shock button once as instructed. Verify that the analyzer records delivered energy within the facility’s acceptance criteria. Repeat only as permitted by the approved test procedure. Expected outcome: The AED consistently activates the shock control and delivers the advised shock into the analyzer. If the AED passes repeated testing, investigate possible pad, battery, operating-sequence, or event-specific causes before returning it to service. If the button fails to activate or register during testing, stop and escalate the unit for repair.

steps.title: 11. Inspect for Environmental or Physical Damage
steps.instructions: Check for evidence that may explain intermittent button operation: Recent drop or impact. Liquid exposure. Storage outside approved environmental conditions. Excessive heat or cold. Loose enclosure sections. Unusual odor or heat. Previous damage or unresolved repair history. Expected outcome: No environmental or physical condition is found that could compromise shock-button operation. Any evidence of liquid intrusion, enclosure damage, unusual heat, or impact requires removal from service and qualified repair evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the ZOLL AED 3 advised a shock, but pressing the illuminated shock button did not deliver energy.
CCR.Cause: The AED consistently charged during analyzer testing, but the shock button did not register when pressed, indicating a suspected internal shock-control failure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the AED from service, labeled it Out of Service, placed a verified replacement AED at the clinical location, and sent the unit for authorized repair evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Evidence of impact or liquid exposure
Replacement AED location or asset number

title: ZOLL AED 3 Defibrillator - CPR Feedback or Compression Depth Detection Failure
description: Troubleshooting missing, intermittent, or inaccurate CPR compression feedback caused by electrode placement, CPR sensor position, pad connections, surface movement, or accessory failure.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not interrupt clinically indicated CPR to perform extended equipment troubleshooting. If CPR feedback fails during an active resuscitation: Continue chest compressions according to the facility’s resuscitation protocol. Do not delay rhythm analysis or defibrillation solely because CPR feedback is unavailable. Use trained clinical judgment for compression rate, depth, recoil, and hand placement. Obtain another verified AED or monitor/defibrillator when equipment performance is uncertain. Expected outcome: CPR and defibrillation continue without depending on potentially inaccurate feedback. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the device has been removed from active patient use.

steps.title: Confirm the Reported Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint involves: No compression-depth bar or visual movement; No compression-rate feedback; Missing or delayed “Push Harder” or corrective prompts; Feedback that appears only intermittently; Depth readings that do not match the applied compressions; CPR feedback that stops when the cable or pads are moved. Record whether defibrillation prompts, rhythm analysis, audio prompts, and the display otherwise function normally. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to CPR feedback rather than a broader AED malfunction.

steps.title: Verify the Correct Electrodes Are Installed
steps.instructions: Confirm that genuine, compatible ZOLL CPR Uni-padz are connected to the AED 3. The AED 3 uses a sensor incorporated into the CPR electrode assembly to measure compression movement and provide rate-and-depth feedback. Standard electrodes without the required CPR sensor may not provide this function. Inspect the package and electrodes for: Correct product identification; Expiration date; Opened or damaged packaging; Visible cable damage; Contamination or moisture; Signs that the pads were previously used. Expected outcome: The correct, unopened, in-date electrode set is available. If an incorrect, expired, damaged, or previously used set is found, replace it and repeat the functional evaluation. If feedback returns, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Inspect the Electrode Connector
steps.instructions: Disconnect and reconnect the CPR Uni-padz connector according to normal operating procedures. Check for: Partial insertion; Debris or moisture; Bent, recessed, or damaged contacts; A cracked connector housing; Cable strain near the connector; Intermittent operation when the connector is gently handled. Do not probe, bend, or attempt to repair connector contacts. Expected outcome: The electrode connector is fully seated and remains stable without intermittent feedback. If reseating restores consistent CPR detection, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify CPR Sensor and Hand-Placement Position
steps.instructions: Using an approved CPR training manikin, position the electrodes and CPR sensor exactly as shown on the electrode illustrations. The rescuer’s hands must apply compressions over the marked hand-placement indicator containing the sensor. The sensor detects compression movement and sends the information to the AED for processing. Check that: The sensor is centered over the intended compression location. Compressions are applied directly over the marked indicator. The sensor is not folded, twisted, displaced, or trapped beneath another item. The electrode cable is not pulling the sensor away from the compression area. Expected outcome: Compression activity produces a responsive depth display and appropriate feedback prompts. If correcting sensor position restores feedback, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Confirm Proper Pad Adhesion
steps.instructions: Verify that the electrodes and CPR sensor assembly lie flat against the manikin surface. Look for: Lifted edges; Air pockets; Wrinkled adhesive; Contamination on the contact surface; Excessive cable tension; Poor contact caused by an uneven or inappropriate test surface. Do not reuse clinical electrodes after opening them solely for repeated troubleshooting unless permitted by facility policy and manufacturer instructions. Expected outcome: The electrode assembly remains securely positioned throughout compressions. If poor adhesion is present, test with an approved replacement set. If feedback becomes reliable, document the original electrodes as the cause and stop.

steps.title: Evaluate the Test Surface and Manikin
steps.instructions: Test CPR feedback only on an appropriate CPR manikin or manufacturer-approved test setup. A soft mattress, unstable stretcher, moving surface, rigid tabletop without chest travel, or unsuitable simulator can produce misleading compression-depth results because the sensor measures movement during compressions. Place the manikin on a stable surface and ensure it provides realistic chest displacement. Expected outcome: Compression feedback changes consistently as compression depth and rate are varied. If the AED responds correctly on an appropriate setup, the device is functioning as expected and the original test method or surface likely caused the complaint.

steps.title: Verify Adult or Child Mode
steps.instructions: Confirm that the selected patient mode matches the intended functional test. The AED 3 uses CPR Uni-padz for adult and child rescue, with pad repositioning and selection of the appropriate operating mode. Check that: Adult mode is selected for an adult CPR test. Child mode is selected only when evaluating the pediatric configuration. The pads are arranged according to the illustrations for the selected mode. The reported issue is not simply a difference in the displayed feedback behavior between modes. Expected outcome: The displayed mode and electrode placement match the test configuration. If correcting the mode or pad arrangement restores expected feedback, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: Check Audio and Display Operation
steps.instructions: Observe the AED during a simulated rescue sequence. Confirm whether: The compression-depth bar is visible. The CPR timer advances. The metronome or CPR prompts are audible. Corrective prompts occur when compression depth or rate is intentionally varied. The screen remains responsive and readable. Audio volume is adequate. The AED 3 provides visual compression-depth information and real-time CPR guidance through its Real CPR Help technology. Expected outcome: Both visual and audible CPR guidance respond appropriately. If visual feedback works but audio does not, troubleshoot the issue as an alarm-speaker or voice-prompt failure rather than a compression-detection failure.

steps.title: Test With a Known-Good Electrode Set
steps.instructions: When available, connect a compatible, in-date electrode set known to function correctly. Repeat the test using: The same AED; The same approved manikin; The same surface; Consistent pad positioning; Comparable compression technique. Expected outcome: The known-good electrodes provide stable rate-and-depth feedback. Interpretation: If the known-good set works, remove the original electrode set from service. If both sets fail in the same manner, suspect an AED connector, signal-processing, software, display, or internal hardware problem. Do not repeatedly open new clinical electrode packages unless the test is necessary and authorized.

steps.title: Restart and Review Readiness Status
steps.instructions: Disconnect the test electrodes, power the AED off, wait briefly, and restart it according to normal operating procedures. Observe: Startup behavior; Readiness indicator; Error messages; Audible alerts; Battery condition; Whether the electrode connection is recognized; Whether the problem returns during a controlled retest. Expected outcome: The AED starts normally, indicates readiness, recognizes the electrodes, and provides consistent CPR feedback. If a readiness failure, service message, or diagnostic code appears, record it exactly and discontinue field troubleshooting.

steps.title: Compare the Complaint With Stored Event Information
steps.instructions: When authorized and available, review the applicable rescue or test record using the facility’s approved ZOLL data-management process. Event information may help determine whether compression activity was recorded even though the rescuer reported that feedback was not displayed or heard. ZOLL identifies CPR rate and compression-depth information as part of AED rescue-event reporting capabilities. Expected outcome: The record helps distinguish among: No compression signal received; Compression data recorded but not displayed; Audio feedback failure; Intermittent electrode or connector operation; Incorrect user or test setup. Do not alter configuration settings or software unless authorized by the facility and supported by current ZOLL service documentation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the ZOLL AED 3 displayed no compression-depth feedback and did not provide corrective CPR prompts during a readiness drill.
CCR.Cause: Testing found that the CPR Uni-padz sensor was displaced from the marked compression location and did not remain flat against the manikin.
CCR.Resolution: Repositioned the electrode assembly on an approved CPR manikin, repeated the simulated rescue sequence, and verified stable compression-depth, rate, timer, visual, and audio feedback.

helpfulDetails: CPR Uni-padz product and expiration information
Intermittent response when the cable was moved

title: ZOLL AED 3 Defibrillator - Audio Prompts Missing, Weak, or Distorted
description: Troubleshooting absent, unclear, weak, intermittent, or distorted voice prompts and metronome tones caused by power, obstruction, damage, configuration, or speaker failure.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot unreliable audio while the AED is assigned as the only available defibrillator for an active emergency. If the problem is discovered during patient care: Notify the responding clinical team. Obtain another verified AED or monitor/defibrillator immediately. Continue CPR and follow the replacement device’s instructions. Do not rely only on the AED 3 display when voice instructions, warning prompts, or shock-related audio cannot be heard clearly. Expected outcome: Patient care no longer depends on an AED with unreliable rescue prompts. The AED 3 uses coordinated visual and audio prompts to guide the rescue sequence, and its front speaker also provides CPR metronome tones and service-related prompts.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Audio Failure
steps.instructions: Power on the AED in a quiet, nonclinical area and determine whether the issue involves: No voice prompts. Prompts that are unusually quiet. Crackling, buzzing, or distorted speech. Intermittent audio. Missing metronome tones. Audio that stops after startup. Audio prompts that do not match the displayed text. Record whether the display continues to show the expected rescue messages. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly identified as a general speaker problem, intermittent problem, or specific missing prompt.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Reported Behavior Is Not Normal
steps.instructions: Confirm which pads and operating mode were used when the complaint occurred. Real CPR Help audio prompts such as compression coaching are not enabled in Child Mode. The absence of those particular prompts with pediatric pads does not by itself indicate a speaker failure. Expected outcome: Normal pediatric-mode behavior is not mistaken for an audio malfunction. If the reported concern only involved missing CPR coaching in Child Mode, document the finding and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Speaker Area
steps.instructions: Examine the speaker opening on the front of the AED for: Tape, labels, or protective film. Dust or dried contamination. Fluid residue. Damage to the enclosure. A carrying case or accessory covering the opening. Evidence that liquid entered the speaker area. Remove only loose external obstruction using an approved cleaning method. Do not insert tools, swabs, compressed air, or liquid into the speaker opening. Expected outcome: The speaker grille is clean, dry, open, and physically undamaged. If clearing an external obstruction restores clear audio, complete functional verification and stop.

steps.title: 5. Check the Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Review the battery indication and check for: A low-battery message. A battery near or beyond its install-by date. Corrosion, contamination, or damage at accessible battery contacts. A battery that is not fully seated. Remove and reinstall the battery according to normal approved handling practices. When available, test with a compatible, in-date, known-good ZOLL AED 3 battery. The AED may issue CHANGE BATTERY when its self-test identifies a battery condition insufficient for patient use. Expected outcome: The AED powers normally with a verified battery and produces clear startup audio. If a known-good battery resolves the problem, replace the defective battery, repeat testing, and stop.

steps.title: 6. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: Turn the AED off, wait approximately 30 seconds, and restart it in a quiet area. Observe: Startup voice prompt clarity. Whether displayed and spoken prompts occur together. Metronome or alert-tone quality. Any delayed, clipped, or intermittent speech. Status-indicator condition. Any displayed failure message. The device should provide a UNIT OK prompt after successfully passing its power-up tests. A UNIT FAILED prompt indicates that the AED failed testing and is not usable for patient care. Expected outcome: Startup completes normally and all audible prompts are clear and intelligible. If audio returns but remains intermittent, continue troubleshooting rather than returning the AED to service.

steps.title: 7. Initiate the Approved Self-Test
steps.instructions: With the device removed from patient use, press and hold the On/Off button for at least five seconds to initiate the self-test and enter AED Management Mode. Confirm: The self-test completes. The green readiness check appears. No service or failure message is displayed. Audible prompts remain clear throughout the process. A green status indicator means the AED passed its last self-test. A blank indicator means the AED failed and is not ready for use. Expected outcome: The AED passes self-test and retains a green readiness indicator. A passed self-test does not override an observed speaker defect. If audio remains weak, missing, or distorted, keep the unit out of service.

steps.title: 8. Compare With a Known-Good AED 3
steps.instructions: When another identically configured AED 3 is available, operate both units in the same quiet environment. Compare: Speech volume. Speech clarity. Metronome tone. Alert tones. Startup prompt timing. Do not use personal preference alone to determine whether the audio is acceptable. The voice prompts must be clearly understandable at a normal rescue working distance. Expected outcome: The affected unit performs comparably to a verified AED 3. If the affected unit is significantly quieter or more distorted, suspect an internal speaker, amplifier, connection, or audio-processing failure.

steps.title: 9. Review Device History and Failure Information
steps.instructions: In AED Management Mode, review available status information and export device history when permitted by facility procedure. Document: Date and time of the reported failure. Most recent self-test result. Battery status. Error codes. Whether the failure was constant or intermittent. Whether it followed impact, cleaning, fluid exposure, or battery replacement. The AED stores self-test results, device status, battery information, and recent error codes in its device history. Expected outcome: Useful diagnostic information is collected for repair evaluation.

steps.title: 10. Complete Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Before returning the AED to service, confirm: Startup speech is present and intelligible. Audio is not weak, distorted, or intermittent. Visual and spoken prompts correspond. Tones and metronome sounds are clear. The self-test passes. The green readiness indicator is displayed. No service message remains. Expected outcome: The AED provides dependable audible and visual rescue guidance. If any audio abnormality remains, stop testing and remove the unit from service.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported that the ZOLL AED 3 powered on, but its voice prompts were very weak and distorted.
CCR.Cause: Speaker opening was unobstructed and the condition remained after battery substitution, restart, and self-test, indicating a suspected internal audio-system failure.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the AED from service, applied an Out of Service label, provided a replacement AED, exported device history, and routed the unit for authorized repair evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Voice prompts, tones, or both affected
Evidence of impact or fluid exposure

title: ZOLL AED 3 Defibrillator - Electrode Package Opened, Damaged, Used, or Expired
description: Identifying and correcting AED readiness problems caused by opened, damaged, previously used, disconnected, missing, or expired CPR Uni-padz electrode packages.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot electrode readiness while the ZOLL AED 3 is the only available defibrillator for an active emergency response. If the electrode problem is discovered during a cardiac-arrest response: Begin or continue CPR according to the facility’s emergency-response procedure. Immediately obtain another verified AED or an unopened, compatible replacement electrode package. Do not delay defibrillation while inspecting damaged or expired supplies. Keep the questionable electrode package available for later evaluation and documentation when practical. Expected outcome: Emergency care continues without depending on electrodes of uncertain condition. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after emergency coverage has been restored.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Electrode Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the CPR Uni-padz package is: Opened or partially unsealed; Punctured, torn, crushed, or wet; Previously applied to a patient; Contaminated with blood, fluids, dirt, or cleaning chemicals; Beyond the printed expiration date; Missing from the AED; Connected improperly; Displaying damaged wires, connectors, or insulation. Expected outcome: The specific reason the electrode set is unsuitable or questionable is identified. ZOLL readiness guidance requires AED electrodes to be present, sealed in their package, and within their expiration date.

steps.title: 3. Do Not Attempt to Reuse or Reseal the Package
steps.instructions: Do not tape, glue, heat-seal, or otherwise attempt to restore an opened electrode package. Do not return previously applied electrodes to service, even when: No shock was delivered; The pads appear clean; Adhesive remains present; The electrodes were applied only briefly; The package was opened accidentally. Expected outcome: A compromised single-use electrode set is permanently removed from service.

steps.title: 4. Verify Electrode Compatibility
steps.instructions: Confirm that the replacement is approved for the ZOLL AED 3. The standard ZOLL AED 3 uses CPR Uni-padz universal electrodes for adult and pediatric rescue. Pediatric treatment is selected using the AED’s Child Mode rather than installing a separate pediatric electrode set. Check the replacement package for: Correct ZOLL AED 3 compatibility; Correct connector configuration; Intact factory seal; Legible labeling; Acceptable expiration date; No punctures, moisture, crushing, or contamination. Expected outcome: A correct, unopened, in-date electrode package is available.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Electrode Connector and Cable
steps.instructions: Without opening the replacement package, inspect the visible cable and connector. Check for: Bent or damaged connector surfaces; Broken locking features; Cuts, pinching, or exposed conductors; Contamination inside the connector; Excessive pulling or strain near the package; Cable trapped under the AED cover or carrying case. Expected outcome: The electrode connection components are intact and undamaged. If damage is found, do not install that electrode set. Obtain another replacement.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the AED Electrode Receptacle
steps.instructions: Examine the AED electrode receptacle externally using adequate lighting. Look for: Foreign material; Bent or recessed contacts; Fluid contamination; Cracked surrounding plastic; Evidence of forced insertion; A connector fragment remaining inside the receptacle. Do not insert metal tools, probes, or cleaning fluids into the receptacle. Expected outcome: The receptacle is visibly clean, dry, and mechanically intact. If physical damage or contamination is present, remove the AED from service and send it for bench evaluation.

steps.title: 7. Install the Replacement Electrodes
steps.instructions: Connect the unopened replacement CPR Uni-padz package according to the AED’s normal storage configuration. Ensure that: The connector is aligned correctly. It is fully seated without excessive force. The cable is routed without sharp bends or pinching. The sealed package remains accessible for emergency removal. The expiration date remains visible for routine inspection. Expected outcome: The replacement electrodes are securely connected and stored without damaging the package or cable.

steps.title: 8. Verify the AED Readiness Indicator
steps.instructions: After installing the replacement electrodes, confirm the AED’s status indicator. The ZOLL AED 3 status indicator provides a quick indication of whether the device passed its most recent self-test and is ready for use. Verify that: The ready indication is displayed. No warning tone is present. No electrode-related warning remains. The AED enclosure and installed supplies appear complete. Allow sufficient time for the AED to recognize the replacement electrodes and complete any applicable readiness check. Expected outcome: The AED returns to its normal ready condition. If the ready indication returns, the electrode problem is resolved. Stop troubleshooting and return the AED according to facility policy.

steps.title: 9. Check the Replacement Electrode Set if the Warning Remains
steps.instructions: If the AED does not return to ready status: Reseat the connector once. Confirm that the replacement package is compatible and in date. Inspect the connector for shipping damage. Try another known-good, unopened, compatible electrode package when available. Verify that the battery and other AED supplies are also installed correctly. Expected outcome: A defective replacement package or incomplete connection is ruled out. If another verified electrode package corrects the condition, remove the first replacement set from stock and document it as defective.

steps.title: 10. Complete a Final Readiness Inspection
steps.instructions: Before returning the AED to service, verify: Green or normal ready status; No audible warning; Unopened and undamaged electrode package; Expiration date acceptable under facility policy; Electrode cable and connector properly stored; Battery installed and within its replacement interval; AED clean, complete, accessible, and free of visible damage. ZOLL describes the AED 3 as using long-life CPR Uni-padz electrodes and a smart battery designed to report readiness-related status. Expected outcome: The complete AED system is ready for emergency deployment.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported that the ZOLL AED 3 electrode package was torn and the AED was not considered ready for emergency use.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found the connected CPR Uni-padz package punctured near the cable entry, making the electrode seal and adhesive condition unreliable.
CCR.Resolution: Removed and discarded the damaged electrode set, installed an unopened in-date CPR Uni-padz package, verified normal ready status, and returned the AED to service.

helpfulDetails: Electrode part number and lot number
Whether the package was opened, torn, wet, contaminated, or used
Whether the electrodes had been applied to a patient
Whether a second electrode package was tested
Disposition of the damaged or expired electrodes

title: ZOLL AED 3 Defibrillator - Pediatric Mode or Pediatric Electrode Recognition Failure
description: Troubleshooting failure to enter Child Mode, recognize pediatric electrodes, display pediatric prompts, or accept compatible pads due to connections, accessories, or controls.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting while the AED 3 is the only defibrillator available for an active pediatric emergency. If pediatric mode or electrode recognition fails during patient care: Notify the responding clinical team immediately. Obtain another verified AED or defibrillator capable of pediatric therapy. Continue CPR and follow the facility’s emergency response procedure. Do not delay clinically indicated resuscitation while investigating equipment behavior. Remove the affected AED from the rescue once a replacement device is available. Expected outcome: Patient care no longer depends on an AED with uncertain pediatric energy selection or rhythm-analysis behavior. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the device is safely removed from patient use.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Power on the AED and document the observed condition: Child button does not illuminate when selected. Child Mode will not activate. Pedi-padz II are connected, but the AED does not announce or display pediatric-pad recognition. The device announces ADULT PADS when pediatric pads are expected. The device displays PLUG IN PADS CABLE, ATTACH CORRECT DEFIB PADS, or REPLACE PADS. The Child button, screen, or prompts respond intermittently. The AED 3 uses lower configured energy settings and a pediatric-specific rhythm-analysis algorithm when operating in Child Mode. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly defined before accessories or the AED are replaced.

steps.title: 3. Confirm Which Electrode Type Is Installed
steps.instructions: Inspect the electrode package and part identification. The AED 3 supports several electrode types, including: CPR Uni-padz for adult or pediatric use when Child Mode is manually activated. Pedi-padz II for pediatric use. CPR-D-padz, CPR Stat-padz, and Stat-padz II for adult use only. Do not assume that an adult-only pad set will automatically place the AED into pediatric operation. Expected outcome: A compatible pediatric-capable electrode set is confirmed. If the wrong electrode type is installed, replace it with the correct compatible set, repeat the operational check, and stop if normal operation returns.

steps.title: 4. Understand the Expected Mode-Selection Behavior
steps.instructions: For CPR Uni-padz: Pediatric operation is selected by pressing the Child button. Reposition the universal electrodes according to the pediatric illustrations on the package. Confirm that the Child button illuminates and pediatric graphics or prompts appear. For Pedi-padz II: Connecting the pads should automatically illuminate the Child button. The AED should identify the connected electrodes as pediatric pads. Expected outcome: The AED responds appropriately for the specific electrode type being tested.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Electrode Package
steps.instructions: Verify that the pads are: Within their expiration date. Unopened and properly sealed. Free from cuts, crushing, punctures, moisture intrusion, or contamination. Specifically labeled as compatible with the ZOLL AED 3. Equipped with an undamaged cable and connector. Do not use opened, previously applied, expired, or visibly damaged electrodes for a readiness test. Expected outcome: The electrode set has no visible condition that could prevent correct identification or operation. If the package is compromised or expired, replace the pads and stop if recognition returns.

steps.title: 6. Check the Pad Cable Connection
steps.instructions: Turn the AED off. Disconnect the electrode connector and inspect: The connector body for cracks or deformation. Contacts for contamination, moisture, corrosion, or foreign material. The cable near the connector for cuts, stretching, or intermittent damage. The AED connector receptacle for debris or physical damage. Reconnect the cable fully and securely without forcing it. Power on the AED and observe for: Child Mode activation. PEDIATRIC PADS recognition. Absence of PLUG IN PADS CABLE or incompatible-pad messages. ZOLL directs users to verify that the pad cable is properly connected when the AED issues a pad-cable prompt. Expected outcome: A loose or incomplete connection is corrected. If recognition becomes stable, complete the readiness check and stop.

steps.title: 7. Test the Child Button With CPR Uni-padz
steps.instructions: With compatible CPR Uni-padz connected and the AED powered on: Press the Child button once. Confirm that the button illuminates. Confirm that the display changes to pediatric placement graphics or instructions. Press the button again only as needed to verify repeatable mode switching. Check for sticking, contamination, physical damage, or delayed response. Do not repeatedly press or strike the control. Expected outcome: Child Mode activates consistently from the front-panel control. If the button remains physically or electronically unresponsive, remove the AED from service.

steps.title: 8. Substitute a Known-Good Compatible Electrode Set
steps.instructions: Install a new, sealed, in-date set of compatible electrodes of the same intended type. Repeat the test: For Pedi-padz II, verify automatic Child button illumination. For CPR Uni-padz, verify manual Child Mode selection. Confirm that no incompatible-pad, replace-pad, or cable prompt appears. The AED may issue ATTACH CORRECT DEFIB PADS when connected pads are incompatible and REPLACE PADS when it detects a problem with the electrode set. Expected outcome: The test determines whether the original electrode package or the AED is responsible. If the known-good pads work correctly, discard or quarantine the failed electrode set according to facility policy and stop.

steps.title: 9. Power-Cycle and Perform a Self-Test
steps.instructions: Turn the AED off, wait briefly, and power it back on. Where permitted by facility procedure, press and hold the On/Off button for at least five seconds to initiate the self-test and enter management mode. Verify: The AED announces UNIT OK. The green readiness check appears. No service message is present. The pads remain recognized. Child Mode still functions correctly after restart. A blank readiness window indicates that the AED failed its last self-test and is not ready for use. Expected outcome: The device completes its self-test and retains correct pediatric-mode operation. If the AED announces UNIT FAILED, lacks the green readiness indicator, or loses recognition again, remove it from service.

steps.title: 10. Perform an Approved Functional Evaluation
steps.instructions: Using an approved ZOLL AED simulator or facility-approved test equipment: Verify normal power-up. Confirm correct pad or simulator recognition. Verify reliable Child Mode activation. Confirm that pediatric mode remains active during the test. Verify that the correct pediatric indications are displayed. Do not deliver test energy into actual disposable pads or improvised loads. Follow only approved performance-verification procedures and test-equipment instructions. Do not open the AED housing or attempt internal control-board or connector repair. Expected outcome: Pediatric-mode selection and electrode-recognition functions operate consistently under controlled conditions. If the failure repeats with known-good accessories and approved test equipment, stop troubleshooting.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the ZOLL AED 3 would not enter Child Mode and did not recognize the connected pediatric electrode set.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found an intermittent connection at the damaged Pedi-padz II cable near the electrode connector; the AED passed testing with a new compatible pad set.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the defective pediatric electrodes, verified automatic Child Mode activation, completed the AED self-test, and confirmed a green readiness indicator before returning the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Exact electrode type and part number

title: ZOLL AED 3 Defibrillator - USB Data Export or Rescue Event Download Failure
description: Troubleshooting failed rescue-event exports caused by USB media, file compatibility, device access, software, computer security, or connection problems.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform data-export troubleshooting while the ZOLL AED 3 is assigned as the only available AED for an active patient-care area. Before beginning: Confirm another verified AED is immediately available. Ensure the AED 3 remains operational and displays its normal ready status. Do not remove the battery, pads, or essential accessories solely to retrieve event data. Follow facility procedures for preserving post-rescue clinical information. Expected outcome: Emergency-response coverage remains available while the device is being evaluated. Continue only after the AED can be safely removed from active readiness.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine which part of the process is unsuccessful: The USB drive is not recognized. The export option is unavailable. No rescue event appears for selection. The export begins but does not complete. A file is created but cannot be opened. RescueNet EventSummary does not detect or import the exported information. The computer blocks access to the USB drive. Record any displayed message and whether the problem occurs with every event or only one rescue record. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to the AED, USB media, exported file, computer, or review software.

steps.title: 3. Verify the AED Is in the Correct Non-Rescue Mode
steps.instructions: Confirm the AED is not in active rescue operation and that Clinical Engineering has entered the appropriate maintenance or data-access function using authorized facility procedures. Do not attempt to export information while: The pads are connected to a patient. A rescue sequence is active. The AED is performing a self-test. The device is displaying another unresolved fault. Expected outcome: The appropriate data-management options become available. If the export option remains unavailable, stop and verify authorized access requirements before proceeding.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the USB Port and Drive
steps.instructions: Remove the USB drive and inspect: The USB connector for bending, contamination, or physical damage. The AED USB port for debris, looseness, or damaged contacts. The drive housing for cracks or signs of liquid exposure. Whether the drive seats fully without excessive force. Do not insert tools into the AED USB port or attempt to straighten internal contacts. Reconnect the drive firmly and retry the export. Expected outcome: The AED recognizes the USB device and permits the export. If successful, verify the exported file before returning the AED to service and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Test With an Approved Compatible USB Drive
steps.instructions: Use a known-good, facility-approved USB flash drive that: Has adequate free storage space. Is not write-protected. Is free of unrelated sensitive information. Uses a file-system format supported by the facility’s ZOLL data-export process. Has been approved under hospital cybersecurity and removable-media policies. Avoid USB hubs, card readers, encrypted drives, adapters, and drives containing bundled security software unless specifically approved. Retry the export using the known-good drive. Expected outcome: The event exports successfully, identifying the original USB drive as incompatible, full, corrupted, or defective. If successful, remove the failed media from use and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 6. Confirm That a Rescue Event Is Stored
steps.instructions: Review the AED’s available event information using the authorized data-access process. Consider whether: The reported activation actually progressed far enough to create a rescue record. A newer event may have affected storage availability. The incorrect date or event was selected. Event information was previously exported or managed under local procedures. The AED’s date and time could make the event appear under an unexpected timestamp. Do not erase, reset, or overwrite event information while investigating a download complaint. Expected outcome: The required rescue event is located and selected for export. If no event is available, document that finding and escalate before performing any action that could alter stored data.

steps.title: 7. Verify the Exported Files on a Computer
steps.instructions: After the AED reports a completed export: Use the operating system’s safe-removal process before disconnecting the USB drive. Connect the drive to an approved hospital computer. Confirm that files or folders were created. Compare the file date and time with the rescue event. Copy the files to the approved secure location before analysis. Do not rename, modify, or open the source files with unrelated applications. The ZOLL AED 3 supports rescue-data review through ZOLL RescueNet EventSummary, and ZOLL identifies USB as a supported method for exporting detailed rescue information. Expected outcome: The exported files are present, readable, and associated with the correct rescue event. If the USB drive is empty despite a completed-export indication, repeat the export once using a different approved drive.

steps.title: 8. Check RescueNet EventSummary and Computer Compatibility
steps.instructions: Confirm that the receiving computer: Has an approved version of RescueNet EventSummary installed. Recognizes the USB drive normally. Allows access to removable media. Has sufficient local storage. Is not blocking the file through endpoint-security software. Is being used under an account with the required permissions. Attempt to import the same file on another approved computer with known-good RescueNet EventSummary software. ZOLL’s current RescueNet EventSummary download page lists support for the ZOLL AED 3 product family. Expected outcome: The event opens on the alternate workstation, identifying the original computer, application installation, permissions, or security controls as the cause. If the file cannot be opened on more than one approved workstation, preserve the original exported files and continue to escalation.

steps.title: 9. Restart and Recheck the AED
steps.instructions: After confirming that no patient is connected and no export is in progress: Exit the data-access function normally. Turn the AED off. Remove the USB drive. Wait briefly. Restart the AED according to normal operating procedures. Confirm the normal ready indication. Reenter the authorized data-access function and retry with a known-good USB drive. Do not remove the battery as a reset method unless directed by approved service documentation or ZOLL technical support. Expected outcome: A temporary software or USB-enumeration condition clears and the export completes. If the AED displays a readiness failure, startup error, or abnormal indicator after restarting, remove it from service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical Engineering was notified that the ZOLL AED 3 would not export the most recent rescue event to a USB flash drive.
CCR.Cause: The original USB drive was not recognized by the AED, while a facility-approved known-good drive was detected and completed the export normally.
CCR.Resolution: Exported and verified the rescue-event files using an approved USB drive, confirmed the AED’s ready status, and removed the defective drive from service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the event appeared in the AED
Whether another USB drive was tested
Whether files appeared on the drive
Whether another computer opened the file
Location of securely preserved event files

title: ZOLL AED 3 Defibrillator - Software Update or Configuration Transfer Failure
description: Troubleshooting failed software updates or configuration transfers caused by battery level, USB media, file naming, file compatibility, access, or connection problems.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform software updates, configuration transfers, or USB troubleshooting while the AED is assigned to an active patient or emergency response. Before beginning: Remove the AED from active clinical service. Provide another verified AED for coverage. Confirm that no patient is connected to the defibrillation pads. Do not connect the AED USB port to a computer or other device while the pads are connected to a patient. Expected outcome: Emergency response coverage remains available, and the AED can be evaluated without affecting patient care. ZOLL specifically warns against USB connection while the pads remain connected to a patient.

steps.title: 2. Record the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Repeat the transfer only far enough to identify and document: The complete displayed message; whether the failure involves software, clinical configuration, Wi-Fi configuration, or certificates; whether the USB device icon appears; the current software version, when available; whether the failure occurred before, during, or after restart; whether another AED accepted the same file. Expected outcome: The troubleshooting path is based on the actual failure rather than a general report.

steps.title: 3. Confirm the Correct Transfer Method
steps.instructions: Use a USB flash drive for configuration transfers and software imports. Configuration files cannot be transferred between AEDs through Wi-Fi. ZOLL identifies configuration export and import as USB functions. Expected outcome: The selected method matches the type of file being transferred. If configuration transfer was being attempted through Wi-Fi, switch to the approved USB method and retry. If successful, stop.

steps.title: 4. Check Battery Capacity Before a Software Update
steps.instructions: Verify that the installed battery has more than 30% remaining capacity. The AED will not permit a software update when battery capacity is below 30%. If battery capacity is low: Install a verified battery with adequate capacity. Confirm that the AED starts normally. Restart the update from the beginning. Expected outcome: The software-update option is available and the update can proceed without a low-battery interruption. If this resolves the problem, complete post-update testing and stop.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the USB Connection Externally
steps.instructions: Remove the USB flash drive and inspect: The flash drive connector; the AED USB receptacle; the rear connector area; the USB cover, if applicable; evidence of bent contacts, contamination, moisture, or physical damage. Do not insert tools into the port or attempt internal connector repair. Reinsert the flash drive fully and confirm that the USB-device icon appears on the display after entering AED Management mode. Expected outcome: The AED recognizes the USB flash drive. If no USB icon appears, test with another known-good compatible flash drive. If neither drive is recognized, remove the AED from service for bench evaluation.

steps.title: 6. Verify USB Flash-Drive Compatibility
steps.instructions: Use a known-good USB flash drive that is compatible with USB 1.1 or USB 2.0. ZOLL specifies USB 1.1 or 2.0 compliance for file import and export. Also confirm that the drive: Has sufficient free storage space; is readable by a workstation; does not contain obvious file-system errors; is not write-protected; is not being connected through an adapter or hub. For export failures, an empty known-good drive is preferred. Expected outcome: The AED detects reliable removable media with enough available space. If replacing the flash drive resolves the issue, verify the completed transfer and stop.

steps.title: 7. Confirm the Correct File Is Present
steps.instructions: For configuration import, verify that the USB drive contains the intended .ini configuration file. For software updates, verify that: The update package came from an authorized ZOLL source. The package is specifically intended for the ZOLL AED 3. The file has not been manually modified. All required package contents were copied completely. The file was not extracted or renamed contrary to ZOLL instructions. An “Unable to save file to device” message may indicate that the required configuration file is not present on the USB drive. Expected outcome: The USB drive contains the correct and complete file for the selected import type. If the file is missing or questionable, obtain a clean authorized copy and retry.

steps.title: 8. Check the Configuration Filename
steps.instructions: Verify that a configuration filename: Ends in .ini; contains no spaces; has not had its extension changed; has not been unintentionally duplicated, such as configuration.ini.ini. ZOLL directs that configuration filenames intended for import must not contain spaces. Expected outcome: The AED can locate and interpret the configuration file. If correcting the filename resolves the issue, verify the transferred settings and stop.

steps.title: 9. Enter AED Management Mode Correctly
steps.instructions: With the USB drive inserted: Press and hold the On/Off button for more than five seconds. Confirm that the USB icon appears. Select the Device Configuration icon. Select Supervisor Access. Enter the authorized supervisor passcode. Select Import Files. Choose Configuration, System Software, or Root Certificates, as applicable. Supervisor access is required to import files from a USB flash drive. Expected outcome: The correct import option becomes available and the desired file is selectable. If access cannot be obtained, verify the approved passcode through the facility AED-program administrator. Do not repeatedly guess or bypass access controls.

steps.title: 10. Select the Correct Configuration Category
steps.instructions: When importing a configuration, confirm that the intended option is selected: Clinical Configuration; Wi-Fi Configuration; Both, when appropriate. A selected item should display a green check before confirmation. Expected outcome: The AED imports the intended settings rather than an unselected or incorrect configuration category. If the device reports that no files were selected, return to the selection screen, select the appropriate item, and retry.

steps.title: 11. Match the Error Message to the External Cause
steps.instructions: Use the displayed message to guide the next action: Unable to save files: Confirm the USB drive is fully inserted and has enough free space. Requested file cannot be found: Confirm that the correct file is present and that the USB drive is recognized. Requested file is out of date: Obtain a configuration version compatible with the receiving AED. Requested file contains invalid data: Replace it with a verified, unmodified source file. Requested file is corrupted: Delete the questionable copy and obtain a fresh authorized file. Configuration files unavailable: Confirm that an exportable configuration exists on the source AED. ZOLL associates these messages with USB recognition, file presence, compatibility, validity, and corruption problems. Expected outcome: The transfer completes after the specific external file or media condition is corrected.

steps.title: 12. Do Not Interrupt a Software Update
steps.instructions: After confirming a software update, allow the process to finish without: Removing the battery; removing the USB drive; pressing the power button; attempting another operation; assuming the blank display indicates failure. ZOLL states that the screen may go blank, the AED will restart, and the process may take up to five minutes. Power must not be removed during this period. Expected outcome: The AED restarts normally after completing the update. If the device does not restart after the stated update period, do not repeatedly power-cycle it. Remove it from service and escalate for technical evaluation.

steps.title: 13. Verify Successful Completion
steps.instructions: Confirm that the AED reports the appropriate successful-transfer message, such as: Files transferred successfully; the expected software-update completion and restart; successful certificate storage, when applicable. Then verify: The expected software version; date and time; clinical configuration settings; adult and child-mode settings; audio and language settings; Wi-Fi configuration, when transferred; readiness indicator; successful self-test; pads and battery status. Expected outcome: The AED is correctly configured, passes its self-test, and returns to a ready condition. If any critical setting is incorrect or the readiness indicator does not show normal status, keep the AED out of service.

steps.title: 14. Compare With a Known-Good Combination
steps.instructions: When available, isolate the failure by testing: The same USB drive and file on another compatible AED 3; a known-good USB drive on the affected AED; a newly exported configuration from a verified source AED; a fresh authorized software package. Interpret the results: One USB drive fails on multiple AEDs: suspect the drive or files. Multiple known-good drives fail on one AED: suspect the AED USB interface or internal software. One configuration fails while another imports: suspect file compatibility or corruption. The update fails at the same point repeatedly: stop and escalate. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to the file, USB media, configuration compatibility, or AED. If the cause is isolated and corrected, repeat the transfer once and complete verification.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the ZOLL AED 3 would not accept a software update or configuration file from the USB flash drive.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found that the configuration filename contained spaces and the original flash drive was not consistently recognized by the AED.
CCR.Resolution: Copied the verified .ini file without spaces to a known-good USB 2.0 drive, completed the import, verified settings, and confirmed a successful self-test and normal readiness indicator.

title: ZOLL AED Plus Defibrillator - Device Will Not Power On
description: Troubleshooting an AED Plus that remains blank or unresponsive due to battery, installation, connection, accessory, environmental, or external damage issues.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot a nonfunctional AED while it is the only defibrillator available for an active emergency. If the failure occurs during patient care: Begin or continue CPR according to facility protocol. Obtain another verified AED or manual defibrillator immediately. Notify the responding clinical team that the AED Plus is unavailable. Do not delay resuscitation while attempting repeated power cycles or battery replacement. Expected outcome: Patient care continues using another functional defibrillator. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the AED Plus has been removed from emergency use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Power Condition
steps.instructions: Press the power button once and closely observe the device. Check for: Display activity; Status-indicator changes; Audible tones or voice prompts; Brief illumination followed by shutdown; Clicking, repeated restarting, or other sounds; Any displayed error message. Expected outcome: The exact failure is identified as complete loss of power, intermittent startup, or startup followed by shutdown. If the device powers on normally, verify readiness and complete an operational check before returning it to service.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Exterior for Damage or Contamination
steps.instructions: Examine the AED Plus for: Cracks, impact damage, or enclosure separation; Liquid intrusion or dried residue; Corrosion around the battery compartment; Unusual odor, heat, swelling, or discoloration; A damaged or stuck power button; Evidence that the unit was dropped or improperly stored. Do not continue powering the device if there is evidence of liquid intrusion, overheating, burning odor, or battery leakage. Expected outcome: No external condition is found that makes continued testing unsafe. If significant damage, liquid intrusion, heat, or odor is present, remove the unit from service and send it for bench evaluation.

steps.title: 4. Check the Status Indicator
steps.instructions: Observe the readiness indicator before opening the battery compartment. Determine whether the indicator shows: A ready symbol; A non-ready condition; No visible indication; An intermittent or abnormal appearance. A non-ready or blank indicator may support a battery, installation, self-test, or internal power concern. Expected outcome: The readiness condition is documented for the work order. Do not return the AED to service solely because the indicator appears normal if the unit will not power on.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Battery Compartment
steps.instructions: Open the battery compartment according to facility procedures and inspect the installed batteries. Check for: Missing batteries; Incorrect battery type; Mixed battery brands or ages; Batteries installed with reversed polarity; Loose or partially seated batteries; Corroded, bent, contaminated, or recessed contacts; Battery leakage or swelling; A damaged battery-compartment cover. The AED Plus uses multiple individual batteries that must be installed correctly as a complete set. A single reversed, weak, missing, or poorly seated battery may prevent startup. Expected outcome: All batteries are present, compatible, correctly oriented, and securely installed. If installation was incorrect, correct it and retest the device. If the AED powers on and completes its self-test successfully, document the correction and stop.

steps.title: 6. Replace the Batteries as a Complete Matched Set
steps.instructions: If battery condition is unknown, expired, depleted, mixed, or questionable, replace all batteries with a complete matched set of approved batteries. Do not: Replace only one or two batteries; Mix new and used batteries; Mix brands, chemistries, or expiration dates; Reuse leaking, corroded, or physically damaged batteries. Install each battery using the polarity markings in the compartment. Expected outcome: The AED receives stable power from a complete, properly installed battery set. After installation, power on the unit and allow it to complete its startup and self-test sequence. If the device powers on normally and passes its checks, proceed with functional verification and stop.

steps.title: 7. Reseat the Battery Set
steps.instructions: If the batteries appear correct but the AED remains unresponsive: Remove the complete battery set. Inspect the battery contacts using adequate lighting. Clean only accessible external contamination using approved procedures. Reinstall the full battery set carefully. Confirm every battery is fully seated. Secure the battery-compartment cover. Attempt one controlled power-on test. Expected outcome: Any poor battery seating or external contact issue is corrected. If the device powers on, complete the required readiness and functional checks before return to service.

steps.title: 8. Check the Power Button Operation
steps.instructions: Press and release the power button while observing its mechanical movement. Confirm that the button: Moves normally; Is not jammed, recessed, cracked, or unusually loose; Is not obstructed by dirt, adhesive, or enclosure damage; Produces consistent mechanical feedback. Do not pry, disassemble, or apply excessive force to the control. Expected outcome: The external power control operates mechanically without visible damage. A damaged or non-moving button requires repair evaluation.

steps.title: 9. Disconnect Nonessential External Accessories
steps.instructions: Inspect the electrode cable and any externally connected accessories for damage, contamination, or improper seating. When safe and permitted by facility procedures, disconnect questionable external accessories and repeat one startup attempt. Do not repeatedly connect and disconnect accessories or perform testing that could damage the connector. Expected outcome: An externally damaged or improperly connected accessory is ruled out as a contributing factor. If the AED powers on after removing a damaged accessory, replace the accessory and complete operational testing.

steps.title: 10. Consider Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm the AED has not recently been exposed to: Extreme cold or heat; Condensation; High humidity; Water; Direct sunlight inside a vehicle; Storage outside the manufacturer’s operating conditions. Allow the device to stabilize in a controlled indoor environment before testing when temperature or condensation may be involved. Do not apply external heat or attempt to dry internal components by opening the enclosure. Expected outcome: Temporary environmental conditions are ruled out. If condensation or liquid exposure is suspected, remove the device from service for inspection.

steps.title: 11. Perform a Controlled Startup Verification
steps.instructions: With a verified complete battery set installed: Confirm the enclosure and battery compartment are secure. Press the power button once. Observe the display, indicator, speaker, and startup sequence. Allow the AED to complete its self-test. Record any prompt, warning, or error message. Expected outcome: The AED powers on, completes its startup checks, and indicates readiness. If the device starts but shuts down, restarts, freezes, or reports a fault, do not return it to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the ZOLL AED Plus display remained blank and the unit did not respond when the power button was pressed.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found a mixed set of depleted batteries, including one battery installed with reversed polarity.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the mismatched batteries, installed a complete approved matched battery set, verified correct polarity, and confirmed successful startup, self-test, audio prompts, display operation, and ready status.

helpfulDetails: Battery manufacturer, type, date, and condition
