title: ZOLL AED Plus Defibrillator - Shock Will Not Deliver After Shock Advised
description: Troubleshooting failed shock delivery caused by model operation, shock-button timing, electrode connection, battery condition, readiness faults, or internal therapy failure.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting while the AED Plus is required for an active resuscitation. If a shock is advised but not delivered: Continue CPR according to the facility’s emergency-response protocol. Obtain another verified AED or defibrillator immediately. Transfer defibrillation capability to the replacement device as soon as possible. Do not delay resuscitation by repeatedly testing the questionable AED. Keep everyone clear whenever the device may be charged. Expected outcome: CPR and defibrillation remain available without relying on equipment with uncertain therapy delivery. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the AED has been removed from patient use.

steps.title: 2. Identify Whether the AED Is Semi-Automatic or Fully Automatic
steps.instructions: Confirm the exact AED Plus version. Semi-automatic AED Plus: The rescuer must press the flashing shock button after the “Shock Advised” and “Press Flashing Shock Button” prompts. Fully automatic AED Plus: The device automatically delivers the shock after its countdown without requiring the shock button to be pressed. Expected outcome: The reported behavior is compared with the correct operating sequence for that specific version. A fully automatic unit should not be classified as having a failed shock button merely because the button was not used.

steps.title: 3. Document the Exact Rescue Sequence
steps.instructions: Obtain the operator’s description and available event data. Record whether: “Shock Advised” was heard or displayed. The shock button illuminated or flashed. A countdown occurred. “Release Shock Button” was announced. “Shock Delivered” was announced. The device returned to CPR prompts without confirming a shock. The unit displayed “Unit Failed,” “Change Batteries,” or another warning. Anyone continued touching or moving the patient during analysis or charging. Expected outcome: Clinical Engineering can distinguish an operating-sequence issue from an actual failure to discharge.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Readiness Indicator
steps.instructions: With the AED turned off, inspect the status-indicator window near the handle. A green check indicates the unit passed its readiness checks. A red X or periodic beeping indicates that the AED should not remain in service. ZOLL instructs users not to place the AED Plus in service when the red X is displayed or the unit is beeping. Expected outcome: The unit shows a green check and is not beeping. If a red X or beeping condition is present, remove the AED from service and continue only with controlled bench evaluation.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the AED and Shock Button Externally
steps.instructions: Check the enclosure and shock button for: Cracks, impact damage, or liquid intrusion. A button that is stuck, recessed, loose, or physically obstructed. Contamination around the button. Damage to the front overlay or indicator lights. Evidence that the unit was dropped during the rescue. Press the button only during an approved simulated test when the analyzer and AED indicate that it is safe to do so. Expected outcome: The button moves normally, returns after release, and has no visible damage. If the control is physically damaged or remains stuck, stop troubleshooting and remove the AED from service.

steps.title: 6. Check the Electrode Cable Connection
steps.instructions: Confirm that the electrode cable connector is fully seated in the AED. Inspect for: A loose or partially inserted connector. Bent, recessed, contaminated, or damaged contacts. A cut, crushed, or sharply kinked cable. Damage where the cable enters the connector. A “Plug in Cable” prompt. ZOLL directs that the electrode cable remain connected to the AED Plus and identifies checking the cable connection as part of readiness troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The compatible ZOLL electrode cable is fully connected and no cable prompt occurs. If reseating the cable corrects the simulated failure and the AED passes all required testing, document the correction and stop.

steps.title: 7. Inspect the Electrode Package and Pads
steps.instructions: Verify that the connected electrodes are: Compatible with the AED Plus. Within their expiration date. Unopened before the reported rescue, unless they were used during that event. Free from tears, punctures, moisture, or damaged packaging. Appropriate for the patient category. Properly adhered during the reported event. For controlled retesting, use an approved defibrillator analyzer and the appropriate test adapter or manufacturer-approved test electrodes. Do not deliver a test shock into unused clinical pads. Expected outcome: The AED recognizes the connected test interface without electrode or connection warnings. If replacing a damaged or expired accessory resolves the issue and the unit passes verification, document the result and stop.

steps.title: 8. Check Battery Condition and Battery History
steps.instructions: Review whether the AED issued a “Change Batteries” prompt or showed signs of weak power during charging. Confirm that: All ten batteries are the approved type specified for the unit. Batteries were installed as a complete matched set. Old and new batteries were not mixed. Battery contacts are clean and undamaged. No corrosion or leakage is present. The battery-replacement date is within the facility’s established interval. ZOLL specifies replacing all ten batteries together and not mixing old batteries with new ones. Expected outcome: The AED powers normally without battery prompts or abnormal resets. If battery replacement is required, replace the entire set according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Do not replace only selected cells.

steps.title: 9. Power-Cycle and Perform the Manual Self-Test
steps.instructions: With the AED disconnected from any patient: Turn the unit off. Wait briefly. Press and hold the ON/OFF button for more than five seconds to initiate the manual test. Listen for the “Unit OK” message. Turn the unit off after the test. Wait approximately two minutes. Confirm that the green check returns and no beeping occurs. ZOLL recommends removing the unit from service when it repeatedly fails the manual self-test. Expected outcome: The AED announces “Unit OK,” completes the test, and returns to a green readiness indication. If the self-test fails, stop and escalate the unit for repair.

steps.title: 10. Test Shock Delivery With an Approved Defibrillator Analyzer
steps.instructions: Only qualified Clinical Engineering personnel should perform this step in a controlled bench area. Using an electrically compatible, calibrated defibrillator analyzer and approved connection method: Connect the AED to the analyzer. Select a rhythm that the analyzer presents as shockable. Allow the AED to complete its analysis. Confirm that “Shock Advised” occurs. For a semi-automatic unit, verify that the shock button flashes and press it only when prompted. For a fully automatic unit, verify the countdown and automatic discharge. Confirm that the analyzer detects the delivered shock. Verify delivered energy and sequence against the facility’s approved acceptance criteria and current manufacturer documentation. Repeat only as required by the approved test procedure. Do not touch the analyzer connections, AED electrodes, or conductive surfaces while the device is charging or discharging. Expected outcome: The AED delivers therapy at the correct point in the rescue sequence, the analyzer detects the discharge, and no fault occurs. If the unit advises a shock but does not discharge into the analyzer, remove it from service. Do not open the enclosure or attempt board-level repair.

steps.title: 11. Confirm Final Readiness
steps.instructions: After testing: Disconnect the analyzer. Install a sealed, compatible, unexpired electrode package. Confirm the electrode cable is connected. Turn the AED on and verify the expected pad-identification and “Unit OK” prompts. Turn the AED off. Wait for the green check to return. Confirm the AED is not beeping. Verify that all required accessories are present. Expected outcome: The AED passes functional testing and displays normal ready status. Return the unit to service only when the reported failure has been explained or corrected and all required tests pass.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the ZOLL AED Plus announced “Shock Advised,” but no shock was delivered when the flashing shock button was pressed.
CCR.Cause: Bench testing reproduced the failure; the AED recognized a shockable analyzer rhythm and illuminated the shock button, but no discharge was detected despite verified electrodes and a complete new battery set.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the AED Plus from service, labeled it Out of Service, provided a replacement AED, and forwarded the unit for authorized therapy-circuit evaluation.

title: ZOLL AED Plus Defibrillator - ECG Analysis Will Not Start or Complete
description: Troubleshooting delayed, interrupted, or incomplete ECG analysis caused by electrode contact, patient movement, environmental interference, connections, batteries, or device faults.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting while the AED Plus is required for an active resuscitation. If ECG analysis will not begin or repeatedly stops during patient care: Continue CPR when instructed by the clinical response protocol. Obtain another verified AED or defibrillator immediately. Do not delay rhythm assessment or clinically indicated defibrillation while repeatedly testing the affected AED. Transfer care to the replacement device as soon as it is available. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without depending on an AED whose rhythm-analysis function is uncertain. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the AED Plus has been removed from active patient use.

steps.title: 2. Record the Exact Analysis Behavior
steps.instructions: Power on the AED in a controlled, nonclinical setting and document: Whether normal voice and visual prompts begin; Whether the device recognizes that electrodes are connected; Whether it repeatedly prompts to attach or check electrodes; Whether “Analyzing” begins and then stops; Whether a “Do Not Touch Patient” or motion-related prompt occurs; Whether the device restarts, shuts down, or displays a red X; Any beeping, error message, or abnormal indicator. Expected outcome: The complaint is narrowed to an electrode-recognition, signal-quality, power, interference, or internal device problem. If the AED displays a red X, continuously beeps, or reports a service condition, stop troubleshooting and remove it from service. ZOLL states that an AED Plus showing a red X or emitting a beeping tone should not be placed in service.

steps.title: 3. Check the Status Indicator and Physical Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect the AED Plus before connecting test accessories. Verify that: The readiness indicator displays the green check; The enclosure is not cracked, wet, crushed, or contaminated; No loose components are heard inside the housing; The electrode connector and cable receptacle are clean and undamaged; There is no unusual heat, odor, corrosion, or evidence of liquid intrusion. Expected outcome: The AED appears externally intact and has passed its most recent self-test. A red X, physical damage, liquid intrusion, unusual heat, or burnt odor requires immediate removal from service.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Electrode Connection
steps.instructions: Confirm that the electrode cable connector is fully seated in the AED Plus. Inspect the connector for: Partial insertion; Bent, recessed, contaminated, or damaged contacts; Cracked connector housing; Pinched, cut, stretched, or exposed cable conductors; Strain damage where the cable enters the connector or electrode package. Disconnect and reconnect the electrode connector only when the device is not attached to a patient. Expected outcome: The connector seats securely and the AED no longer gives an attach-electrodes prompt. If reseating the connector resolves the problem, complete functional verification and stop.

steps.title: 5. Confirm Electrode Compatibility and Condition
steps.instructions: Check that the connected electrodes are approved for the AED Plus and appropriate for the intended patient category. Verify that the electrode package is: Unopened before use; Within its expiration date; Dry and undamaged; Not previously applied or used; Free of punctures, tears, or crushed areas. Do not test clinical readiness using expired, opened, dried, or damaged electrodes. Expected outcome: A compatible electrode set of known condition is available for evaluation.

steps.title: 6. Substitute a Known-Good Electrode Set
steps.instructions: Using an approved simulator or manufacturer-compatible test arrangement, connect a known-good, in-date electrode set. Do not repeatedly open clinical electrode packages solely for troubleshooting unless permitted by facility procedure. Observe whether the AED: Recognizes the electrodes; Advances to rhythm analysis; Completes the analysis cycle; Provides the expected shock-advised or no-shock-advised result from the simulator. Expected outcome: Analysis completes normally with the known-good electrode set. If the replacement electrodes resolve the problem, replace the defective or questionable electrode set, document the lot and expiration information, and stop.

steps.title: 7. Verify Electrode Contact Conditions
steps.instructions: When reviewing a reported clinical event, determine whether the original electrodes were applied to: Clean, dry, bare skin; The correct anatomical positions; A chest without excessive hair beneath the adhesive area; Skin free of lotion, medication patches, moisture, or heavy contamination; Areas away from implanted-device prominence when practical. Poor adhesion or high electrode impedance can prevent the AED from obtaining a usable ECG signal. ZOLL directs users to apply fresh, undamaged, in-date electrodes to clean, dry skin. Expected outcome: External contact conditions are confirmed or identified as the likely cause.

steps.title: 8. Eliminate Motion During Analysis
steps.instructions: Confirm that no one is: Performing chest compressions; Touching or moving the patient; Moving the stretcher, bed, or transport vehicle; Adjusting the electrodes or cables; Using powered equipment that causes patient movement. The AED Plus requires the patient to remain as motionless as possible during ECG analysis. Expected outcome: Analysis completes when motion and handling stop. If eliminating motion resolves the issue, no device repair may be necessary. Document the event as motion artifact and verify normal operation before return to service.

steps.title: 9. Remove Environmental Electrical Interference
steps.instructions: Move the AED and test setup away from possible interference sources, including: Two-way radios; High-power radio transmitters; Cellular devices placed directly beside the AED; Electrosurgical equipment; Powered beds or transport systems; Damaged extension cords or power equipment; Other electronic devices connected to the simulated patient circuit. ZOLL warns that high-power radio-frequency sources may cause incorrect rhythm interpretation and advises turning off nearby cellular phones and two-way radios when interference is suspected. Expected outcome: The ECG signal stabilizes and analysis completes without repeated interruption.

steps.title: 10. Check the Battery Installation and Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect the AED Plus battery compartment according to facility procedures. Verify that: All required batteries are installed; Batteries are the correct approved type; All batteries are from the same replacement set; Battery contacts are clean and free of corrosion; No battery is swollen, leaking, reversed, or physically damaged; The battery compartment closes securely. Do not mix old and new batteries. Expected outcome: The AED powers consistently without dim prompts, restarts, shutdowns, or low-battery indications. If battery condition is questionable, replace the complete battery set according to the approved maintenance procedure and repeat the functional check.

steps.title: 11. Perform a Controlled Functional Test
steps.instructions: Using an approved AED analyzer or ECG simulator: Connect the compatible test load or electrode adapter. Power on the AED Plus. Allow it to recognize the simulated patient connection. Select a stable test rhythm. Confirm that analysis starts without repeated electrode prompts. Verify that the AED completes analysis and produces the correct rhythm decision. Repeat with a second appropriate simulated rhythm when required by facility procedure. Do not discharge the AED without an approved analyzer or test load. Expected outcome: The AED consistently completes analysis and correctly classifies the supplied test rhythms. If analysis remains intermittent or fails with known-good accessories and a stable simulator signal, suspect an internal acquisition, connector, processing, or power-related fault.

steps.title: 12. Verify Final Readiness
steps.instructions: After corrective action: Confirm successful startup; Confirm the green readiness indicator; Verify electrode recognition; Complete the facility’s functional and safety checks; Install an unopened, compatible, in-date clinical electrode package; Confirm the battery compartment and enclosure are secure; Return the AED to service only when all required tests pass. Expected outcome: The AED is fully operational, properly stocked, and ready for emergency deployment.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the ZOLL AED Plus repeatedly announced electrode prompts and would not complete ECG rhythm analysis.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found an intermittently open electrode cable near the connector, preventing the AED from receiving a stable simulated ECG signal.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the damaged electrodes, installed a new compatible electrode set, verified successful analysis using an AED analyzer, confirmed the green readiness indicator, and returned the unit to service.

title: ZOLL AED Plus Defibrillator - Shock Button Not Responding
description: Troubleshooting a shock button that does not illuminate, register, or deliver an advised shock due to timing, obstruction, power, pads, or control failure.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting during an active cardiac-arrest response. If the shock button does not respond during patient care: Continue CPR according to the emergency-response protocol. Obtain another verified AED or manual defibrillator immediately. Do not delay resuscitation by repeatedly pressing or testing the button. Transfer defibrillation capability to the replacement device as soon as possible. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without relying on an AED with uncertain shock-delivery capability. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the AED Plus has been removed from patient use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Whether the Unit Is Semi-Automatic
steps.instructions: Verify the exact AED Plus version. A semi-automatic AED Plus instructs the rescuer to press the flashing shock button. A fully automatic AED Plus delivers an advised shock automatically following its countdown and does not require the operator to press the button. Expected outcome: The reported behavior is compared with the correct operating mode. If the unit is fully automatic and completes the countdown normally, the lack of manual button response is not a malfunction.

steps.title: 3. Document the Exact Button Behavior
steps.instructions: Power on the AED in a controlled, nonpatient setting and determine whether: The button is physically stuck or difficult to move. The button remains partially depressed. The button illuminates during the startup sequence. The AED announces “Release shock button.” The button illuminates only when a shock is advised. Pressing the button produces any tone, prompt, or display change. The unit shows a red X, emits periodic beeping, or announces “Unit failed.” Do not attempt to create a shockable condition using a person or improvised test setup. Expected outcome: Clinical Engineering can distinguish a mechanical button problem from a device-state, power, or readiness problem.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Shock Button Externally
steps.instructions: With the AED powered off, inspect the button and surrounding panel for: Dirt, dried fluid, adhesive, or cleaning residue. Cracks, punctures, or impact damage. A distorted or lifted overlay. Foreign material around the button edge. Evidence that the button remains depressed. Signs of liquid intrusion. Gently press and release the button without using tools. It should move normally and return without sticking. Expected outcome: The button is unobstructed and mechanically returns to its normal position. If external contamination is present, clean the surface using an approved method. Do not flood the button area or introduce liquid into the enclosure.

steps.title: 5. Check the Readiness Indicator
steps.instructions: Confirm the status indicator displays the green check and that the unit does not emit periodic beeping while off. ZOLL directs users not to place the AED Plus in service when the indicator displays a red X or the device is beeping. Expected outcome: The AED passes its readiness checks before shock-button operation is evaluated. If a red X or beeping condition is present, troubleshoot the readiness failure before assuming the button alone is defective.

steps.title: 6. Perform a Manual Self-Test
steps.instructions: Press and hold the On/Off button for more than five seconds to initiate the manual self-test. Observe for: “Unit OK.” “Unit failed.” “Release shock button.” Battery prompts. Red-X status. Abnormal startup behavior. ZOLL recommends removing the AED from service if it repeatedly fails the manual self-test. Expected outcome: The AED completes the self-test and reports normal readiness. If the unit announces “Release shock button” when no one is pressing it, the control may be stuck or internally activated. Remove the AED from service.

steps.title: 7. Check the Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm that the AED starts normally and does not announce “Change batteries.” When battery replacement is required: Replace all 10 batteries together. Do not mix old and new batteries. Use the battery type specified by ZOLL for the applicable AED Plus configuration. Follow the facility’s approved battery-replacement procedure. The current ZOLL operator guidance specifies replacing all batteries at the same time when prompted. Expected outcome: Adequate battery power is available for charging and control operation. If fresh approved batteries correct the problem, complete the operational verification and return the unit to service only after all tests pass.

steps.title: 8. Inspect the Electrode Connection and Package
steps.instructions: Confirm that: The electrode connector is fully seated. The cable and connector are not damaged. The electrode package is sealed, compatible, and within expiration. No bent, contaminated, or recessed connector contacts are visible. The AED does not announce “Plug in cable.” The AED will not progress normally through analysis and shock preparation when the electrode connection is incomplete. ZOLL recommends keeping the electrode cable connected to the unit. Expected outcome: The AED recognizes the connected electrode assembly without connection prompts. If reseating or replacing a defective electrode set resolves the issue, stop and complete the required readiness verification.

steps.title: 9. Confirm the Button Is Being Tested at the Correct Time
steps.instructions: On a semi-automatic AED Plus, the shock button is intended to be pressed only after: Pads are connected to an appropriate defibrillator analyzer or approved simulator. The AED completes rhythm analysis. A shockable rhythm is detected. The AED announces “Shock advised.” The shock button flashes. The rescuer is instructed to press the flashing button. The button may not register during startup, CPR prompts, ECG analysis, a no-shock-advised condition, or after the stored energy has been internally discharged. Expected outcome: The complaint is not caused by pressing the control outside the permitted shock-delivery window.

steps.title: 10. Test With an Approved Defibrillator Analyzer
steps.instructions: Using the facility’s approved defibrillator analyzer and applicable ZOLL test adapter or simulation setup: Connect the AED according to the analyzer manufacturer’s instructions. Select an appropriate shockable rhythm. Power on the AED. Allow the unit to complete analysis. Confirm the AED announces “Shock advised.” Verify that the shock button flashes. Press the center of the button once. Confirm the analyzer records an energy discharge. Verify the AED announces “Shock delivered.” Keep all personnel clear of conductive test connections during discharge. Expected outcome: The button registers and the AED delivers energy within the approved test setup. If the button flashes but does not register, do not repeatedly force it or open the enclosure. Remove the unit from service.

steps.title: 11. Evaluate the Test Result
steps.instructions: Use the observed sequence to narrow the cause: Button does not flash: The AED may not have reached the shock-ready state. Recheck the simulated rhythm, pads, battery condition, self-test results, and device prompts. Button flashes but will not depress normally: Suspect external mechanical damage or contamination. Button depresses but no response occurs: Suspect a button-switch, control-interface, charging, or internal therapy fault. AED says “Release shock button” without the button being pressed: Suspect a stuck or falsely activated shock control. Button works intermittently: Treat intermittent operation as a failure because reliable shock delivery cannot be assured. Shock is recorded normally: The reported issue may have resulted from incorrect timing, failure to reach shock-ready status, or an accessory-related condition. If testing resolves the issue, complete all required functional, readiness, and electrical-safety checks before returning the AED to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the ZOLL AED Plus announced “Shock advised,” but pressing the flashing shock button did not deliver therapy.
CCR.Cause: The shock button illuminated during analyzer testing but did not register when pressed, indicating a failed or intermittent shock-control assembly.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the AED Plus from service, labeled it Out of Service, provided a replacement AED, and forwarded the unit for authorized repair.

title: ZOLL AED Plus Defibrillator - CPR Feedback or Compression Detection Failure
description: Troubleshooting missing, intermittent, or inaccurate CPR feedback caused by incompatible pads, CPR sensor position, pad connections, surface movement, or accessory damage.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not interrupt clinically indicated CPR to investigate the feedback system during an active resuscitation. If CPR feedback fails during patient care: Continue chest compressions according to the facility’s resuscitation protocol. Do not delay rhythm analysis or defibrillation solely because corrective CPR prompts are unavailable. Use trained clinical judgment for compression rate, depth, recoil, and hand placement. Obtain another verified AED or monitor/defibrillator when overall device performance is uncertain. Expected outcome: CPR and defibrillation continue without depending on unreliable compression feedback. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the AED Plus has been removed from active patient use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint involves: No CPR metronome; No “Push Harder” prompt; No “Good Compressions” prompt; Feedback that starts and stops; Feedback that does not correspond with compression depth; CPR feedback absent while all other AED functions appear normal; Failure to recognize any chest-compression movement. Record the exact prompts, indicator behavior, electrode type, and point in the rescue sequence when the failure occurred. Expected outcome: The complaint is clearly distinguished from an audio, electrode-recognition, or general device failure.

steps.title: 3. Verify That CPR-D-padz Are Installed
steps.instructions: Inspect the connected electrodes and package labeling. The AED Plus CPR monitoring function requires compatible CPR-D-padz with the compression sensor. Standard electrodes or pediatric Pedi-padz II do not provide adult CPR depth feedback. ZOLL states that the CPR monitoring function is intended for adult patients and is not intended for patients under eight years old. Confirm that: The electrodes are labeled CPR-D-padz. The package is unopened and within its expiration date. The central CPR sensor assembly is present. The pads are intended for the AED Plus. No adapter or unsupported electrode configuration is being used. Expected outcome: A sealed, compatible CPR-D-padz set is available. If the wrong electrode type caused the complaint, replace it with the correct accessory, verify readiness, document the correction, and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the CPR-D-padz Package and Sensor
steps.instructions: Without opening a service-ready pad package unnecessarily, inspect it for: Torn, punctured, wet, or partially opened packaging; Crushing or deformation near the CPR sensor; Bent or sharply folded electrode wiring; Loose components inside the package; Contamination or fluid exposure; Expired labeling; Evidence that the pads were previously opened or used. A damaged or expired pad set should not be used for patient care. ZOLL instructs users to apply freshly opened, undamaged electrodes that are within their expiration date. Expected outcome: The electrode package and CPR sensor appear intact. If damaged, opened, used, or expired, replace the CPR-D-padz, verify the green readiness indicator, document the accessory failure, and stop.

steps.title: 5. Check the Electrode Connector
steps.instructions: Verify that the electrode cable connector is: Fully seated in the AED Plus; Straight and not partially disengaged; Free of contamination, moisture, or visible damage; Not being pulled by the way the pads are stored; Connected before performing the readiness evaluation. Inspect the device-side connector externally for bent contacts, damaged plastic, looseness, or foreign material. Do not insert tools into the connector. ZOLL recommends keeping the electrode cable connected to the AED Plus and lists cable attachment as a check when the device displays a readiness fault. Expected outcome: The electrode connection is secure and mechanically stable. If reseating the connector resolves the problem, complete the functional check, return the AED to service only when readiness is normal, document the repair, and stop.

steps.title: 6. Confirm Correct Sensor Placement During Controlled Testing
steps.instructions: Use an approved AED simulator, CPR manikin, and facility-authorized test procedure. Do not test compression feedback on a person. Confirm that the CPR sensor would be positioned: Over the center of the chest; Between the rescuer’s hands and the patient; In the orientation shown on the CPR-D-padz graphics; Flat against the manikin without being tilted or displaced; On a firm testing surface. The CPR-D-padz sensor reports chest-compression motion to the AED Plus. Incorrect sensor placement or movement outside the compression point can prevent accurate feedback. Expected outcome: The sensor remains centered and detects controlled compressions. If repositioning restores consistent feedback, document improper sensor placement as the cause and stop.

steps.title: 7. Check the Test Surface and Manikin
steps.instructions: Place the CPR manikin on a firm, stable surface. Avoid testing on: A mattress without an approved backboard; A soft stretcher surface; A moving cart; A flexible tabletop; A manikin with a damaged or excessively stiff chest mechanism. Confirm that the manikin allows measurable chest displacement and returns fully after each compression. Expected outcome: Compression movement occurs through the sensor rather than being absorbed by the support surface. If changing the surface or manikin resolves the issue, repeat the test for consistency, document the test-condition problem, and stop.

steps.title: 8. Observe the CPR Sequence and Prompts
steps.instructions: Using the simulator and test manikin, advance the AED through its normal rescue sequence until it instructs the rescuer to begin CPR. Verify: The AED enters the CPR interval. The metronome begins when expected. Compression-related prompts respond to changes in depth. Feedback remains consistent during repeated compressions. Other voice and visual prompts remain normal. The AED Plus CPR monitoring function provides a metronome and voice or visual feedback intended to encourage appropriate adult compression rate and depth. Expected outcome: The metronome and corrective prompts operate during the CPR phase. If the device has not entered a CPR interval, absent feedback may be normal rather than a failure.

steps.title: 9. Compare With a Known-Good CPR-D-padz Test Accessory
steps.instructions: When permitted by the facility and ZOLL service procedures, repeat the controlled test using a known-good, compatible CPR-D-padz test accessory or approved training interface. Do not open a patient-use electrode package merely for troubleshooting unless it will be removed from inventory afterward. Interpret the results: Known-good accessory works: The original CPR-D-padz or sensor is defective. Both accessories fail: The AED connector, processing, audio, or internal CPR detection circuit may be defective. Feedback is intermittent when the connector moves: Suspect connector or cable damage. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to either the electrode assembly or the AED. If replacing the accessory resolves the issue, complete the readiness check, document the result, and stop.

steps.title: 10. Check Battery and Readiness Status
steps.instructions: Inspect the AED Plus status indicator. Do not return the AED to service if: A red “X” is displayed; The device is beeping while turned off; A “Change Batteries” prompt occurs; A “Unit Failed” message is heard; The device fails its manual self-test. ZOLL instructs that a unit displaying a red “X” or emitting a warning beep should not be placed in service. If battery replacement is indicated, replace all ten batteries as a complete matched set using the manufacturer-specified type and follow the approved battery-reset procedure. Expected outcome: The AED completes its self-test and shows the green check readiness symbol. If normal readiness and CPR feedback return, document the battery or readiness condition and stop.

steps.title: 11. Perform a Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correcting any accessory, connection, or battery issue: Connect a compatible electrode test accessory. Power on the AED. Confirm the expected “Unit OK” and pad-recognition prompts. Complete the approved simulated rescue sequence. Verify CPR metronome and compression feedback. Power off the unit. Wait for the post-test sequence to complete. Confirm the green check appears and no warning beep is present. ZOLL’s checkout procedure requires successful startup, correct pad recognition, and a green readiness indicator before the AED is placed into service. Expected outcome: CPR feedback functions consistently and the AED returns to normal ready status.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the ZOLL AED Plus did not provide “Push Harder” or “Good Compressions” feedback during CPR.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found that standard adult defibrillation pads without the CPR compression sensor were connected instead of CPR-D-padz.
CCR.Resolution: Installed compatible, in-date CPR-D-padz, completed a simulated rescue and compression-feedback test, and confirmed a green readiness indicator before returning the AED to service.

title: ZOLL AED Plus Defibrillator - Electrode Package Opened, Damaged, Used, or Expired
description: Identifying and correcting AED readiness concerns caused by opened, damaged, used, missing, disconnected, improperly stored, or expired electrode packages.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot questionable electrodes while the AED Plus is the only defibrillator available for an active emergency. If the issue is discovered during patient care: Begin or continue CPR according to facility protocol. Obtain another verified AED or a compatible, unopened replacement electrode package immediately. Do not delay clinically indicated defibrillation while inspecting expired or damaged supplies. Do not apply electrodes that are dried out, contaminated, visibly damaged, or previously used. Expected outcome: Emergency care continues without relying on electrodes of uncertain condition. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after emergency coverage has been restored.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Electrode Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect the electrode package without opening a sealed replacement. Determine whether the package is: Opened or partially unsealed; Torn, punctured, crushed, or wet; Previously used; Missing from the AED; Past its printed expiration date; Discolored, swollen, or otherwise abnormal; Stored outside expected environmental conditions; Connected with a damaged or loose cable. Expected outcome: The exact reason the electrode set is unsuitable or questionable is documented. An opened, used, damaged, or expired package cannot be restored to service. Replace it and stop troubleshooting that electrode set.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Correct Electrode Type
steps.instructions: Confirm that the electrodes are approved and compatible with the AED Plus. Common compatible configurations include: CPR-D-padz for adult patients; Pedi-padz II for pediatric patients when the AED Plus is equipped for pediatric operation. Do not substitute AED 3 CPR Uni-padz or electrodes intended only for another defibrillator model. Check the package labeling, connector style, part number, and facility-approved supply list. Expected outcome: The replacement electrodes are confirmed as compatible with the specific AED Plus configuration. ZOLL identifies CPR-D-padz as the adult electrode system used with the AED Plus and specifies pediatric electrodes for patients under eight years old or under 55 pounds when the device supports pediatric use.

steps.title: 4. Check the Printed Expiration Date
steps.instructions: Read the expiration date directly from the electrode package. Do not rely only on: A handwritten inspection sticker; Inventory software; The AED cabinet label; The previous work order; The expected shelf-life calculation. Remove the package from service when the printed expiration date has passed, even when the package remains sealed and appears normal. Expected outcome: Only electrodes within their manufacturer-marked expiration period remain assigned to the AED. ZOLL states that freshly opened, undamaged electrodes within their expiration date should be used. CPR-D-padz are marketed with a five-year shelf life, but the date printed on the individual package controls replacement.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Sealed Package
steps.instructions: Verify that the foil or protective package is fully sealed. Check for: Open seams; Small punctures; Tears near the cable exit; Moisture intrusion; Crushing or sharp folds; Evidence that the adhesive seal has separated; Chemical residue or contamination; Heat damage or discoloration. Do not press, bend, or manipulate the package excessively during inspection. Expected outcome: The installed electrode package is unopened, dry, intact, and free from visible damage. Replace any questionable package. A compromised seal may allow the conductive gel to dry or become contaminated.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Electrode Cable and Connector
steps.instructions: Check the exposed cable from the package to the AED connector. Look for: Cuts or abrasions; Pinching; Crushed insulation; Exposed conductors; Bent connector components; Contamination; A connector that does not seat securely. Do not open the electrode package to inspect the pads themselves. Expected outcome: The external cable is undamaged and the connector is fully seated. ZOLL directs that the electrode cable remain connected to the AED Plus and be checked when the device displays a red readiness indicator or emits a warning tone.

steps.title: 7. Replace the Questionable Electrode Package
steps.instructions: Obtain a new, facility-approved electrode package. Before installation: Verify compatibility. Confirm the package is sealed. Check the printed expiration date. Inspect the cable and connector. Record the new lot number and expiration date when required by facility policy. Connect the electrode cable securely and place the sealed package inside the AED Plus cover without crushing or sharply bending it. Expected outcome: A compatible, sealed, undamaged, and unexpired electrode package is installed. Do not reuse a package that was opened during a previous rescue, even when the pads were not applied.

steps.title: 8. Perform the AED Plus Setup and Check-Out Test
steps.instructions: After replacing the electrodes: Turn the AED Plus on. Listen for the “Unit OK” message. Verify that the device announces the appropriate adult or pediatric pad type. Turn the AED off. Wait approximately two minutes. Confirm that the green check appears in the status-indicator window. Confirm the AED does not emit a periodic beeping tone. Expected outcome: The AED recognizes the electrode connection, completes its self-test, and returns to a green-check ready condition. ZOLL’s setup procedure instructs the technician to connect the electrode cable, verify the appropriate pad announcement, power the unit off, wait two minutes, and confirm the green readiness check without beeping. If the green check appears and no warning tone is present, return the AED to service according to facility policy and stop.

steps.title: 9. Evaluate a Red “X” or Warning Tone
steps.instructions: If the AED displays a red “X” or beeps after electrode replacement: Confirm the connector is fully inserted. Check that no foreign material is obstructing the connector. Verify that the replacement electrodes are compatible. Repeat the power-on check once. Perform the manufacturer-described manual self-test by holding the On/Off button for more than five seconds. Do not repeatedly cycle or test the device after the condition is confirmed. Expected outcome: The AED returns to a green check, or the failure is confirmed for escalation. ZOLL recommends checking the electrode cable and performing a manual test when the AED Plus shows a red “X” or beeps. If the unit continues to fail, it is to be removed from service.

steps.title: 10. Check Storage and Inventory Conditions
steps.instructions: Determine whether the electrode damage or early replacement was associated with: Excessive heat or cold; Direct sunlight; Water exposure; Cabinet damage; Heavy items placed on the AED; Improper cable routing; Repeated opening of the carrying case; Poor stock rotation; Missing expiration tracking. Correct the external storage or inventory problem before installing additional supplies. Expected outcome: The replacement package is protected from the condition that damaged or prematurely aged the previous electrodes. ZOLL cautions that storage outside the recommended environmental conditions can damage electrode pads or reduce their useful life.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the AED Plus CPR-D-padz package was opened and the device was no longer considered rescue ready.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found the adult electrode pouch partially unsealed with the cable intact, making the disposable electrodes unsuitable for continued service.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the CPR-D-padz with a compatible sealed package within expiration, completed the AED Plus check-out test, and verified the green status check with no warning tone.

helpfulDetails: Whether the package was opened, used, damaged, or wet

title: ZOLL AED Plus Defibrillator - Pediatric Electrode Recognition Failure
description: Troubleshooting failure to recognize compatible Pedi-padz II electrodes or activate pediatric-specific ECG analysis and reduced-energy therapy.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended electrode-recognition troubleshooting during an active pediatric emergency. If the problem occurs during patient care: Continue CPR according to the facility’s emergency-response protocol. Obtain another verified AED or defibrillator immediately. Do not delay rhythm analysis or defibrillation while repeatedly reconnecting questionable electrodes. Transfer care to the replacement device as soon as it is available. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without depending on an AED with uncertain pediatric therapy settings. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the AED Plus has been removed from active use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm That the AED Plus Supports Pedi-padz II
steps.instructions: Inspect the AED Plus housing for the pediatric capability symbol identified by ZOLL. Some earlier AED Plus units are not equipped for pediatric operation and will not function with Pedi-padz II electrodes. ZOLL states that units without the pediatric symbol require an upgrade before pediatric electrodes can be used. Expected outcome: The AED Plus is confirmed as a pediatric-capable version. If the pediatric symbol is absent, stop troubleshooting. Remove the device from pediatric service and contact ZOLL or an authorized service provider regarding upgrade eligibility.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Electrode Type
steps.instructions: Confirm that the connected electrodes are genuine, compatible ZOLL Pedi-padz II pediatric electrodes. Check the package and connector for: “Pedi-padz II” identification; Compatibility with the ZOLL AED Plus; Correct part number or facility-approved equivalent; No indication that the electrodes are trainer pads; No adapter or unauthorized extension cable. Pedi-padz II are intended for pediatric patients younger than eight years or weighing less than 55 pounds, or 25 kilograms. The AED Plus should recognize these electrodes and change to pediatric ECG analysis and pediatric energy settings. Expected outcome: The correct clinical pediatric electrodes are being used. If incorrect or training electrodes are connected, replace them with an unopened compatible set and retest.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Electrode Package
steps.instructions: Check the Pedi-padz II package for: Expiration; Opened or damaged seals; Punctures, crushing, moisture, or contamination; Previous use; Damaged or sharply bent lead wires; Missing or damaged connector contacts. Do not open a sealed clinical electrode package solely for routine troubleshooting unless permitted by facility policy. Use an approved test accessory or replacement set when available. Expected outcome: The electrodes are within expiration and have no visible damage that could affect identification or electrical continuity. If damage or expiration is found, replace the electrodes and stop if recognition is restored.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the AED Electrode Connector
steps.instructions: With the AED removed from service and powered off, inspect the electrode connection area. Look for: Debris or contamination; Bent, recessed, loose, or damaged contacts; Cracked connector housing; Evidence of fluid intrusion; A connector that does not seat securely; Strain or damage where the cable enters the plug. Do not insert tools, probes, or cleaning materials into the connector contacts unless specifically approved by the manufacturer. Expected outcome: The connector is clean, intact, and able to accept the electrode plug fully. If physical damage is present, stop and send the AED for bench evaluation.

steps.title: 6. Reseat the Electrode Connector
steps.instructions: Disconnect the electrode plug by holding the connector body rather than pulling on the cable. Reconnect it firmly and evenly until it is fully seated. Confirm that the connector is not partially inserted or under tension from the electrode cable. Power on the AED and observe the prompts and indicators. Expected outcome: The AED recognizes the connected Pedi-padz II and operates using its pediatric-specific analysis and energy protocol. If recognition returns, inspect the connection for intermittent movement and complete the required operational verification before returning the AED to service.

steps.title: 7. Check the Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Review the AED readiness indicator and listen for battery or service-related prompts. If battery condition is questionable: Confirm all ten batteries are the correct approved type. Verify that the batteries were installed together as a complete set. Inspect the battery compartment for contamination, corrosion, or incorrect orientation. Replace the batteries as a complete matched set according to facility procedure. A weak or unstable power source can interfere with startup, accessory detection, or completion of the self-test. Expected outcome: The AED powers on normally without battery or readiness warnings. If battery replacement corrects the recognition problem, complete an operational check and document the battery-related cause.

steps.title: 8. Test With a Known-Good Compatible Electrode Set
steps.instructions: Using an approved test method, connect a known-good set of compatible Pedi-padz II electrodes. Do not use an opened clinical set on a patient after it has been used for troubleshooting unless its instructions and facility policy specifically allow it. Observe whether: The AED accepts the connector; Electrode-related warnings clear; Pediatric operation is recognized; The device begins its expected startup and analysis sequence; Recognition remains stable when the cable is gently repositioned. Expected outcome: The known-good electrode set is recognized consistently. If the known-good set works, the original electrodes or their connector are defective. Replace the original set. If neither set is recognized, the problem is likely associated with the AED connector, pediatric-recognition circuitry, software configuration, or another internal fault.

steps.title: 9. Perform the Approved Operational Check
steps.instructions: After recognition is restored, complete the facility-approved AED Plus inspection or functional verification. Confirm: Normal readiness indication; No service or battery warning; Correct electrode connection status; Expected audible and visual prompts; Pediatric electrodes are recognized consistently; No intermittent response when the connector is handled normally; Batteries and electrodes remain within replacement dates. Do not perform a live shock test without the manufacturer-approved analyzer, simulator, load, and service procedure. Expected outcome: The AED passes the complete operational check and remains stable. If it passes all required testing, return it to service according to facility policy.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the ZOLL AED Plus did not recognize connected Pedi-padz II pediatric electrodes.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found that the pediatric electrode connector was not fully seated, preventing reliable electrode identification.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated the Pedi-padz II connector, verified pediatric recognition with an approved test setup, completed the AED operational check, and returned the unit to service.

title: ZOLL AED Plus Defibrillator - Display, Pictogram, or Status Light Failure
description: Troubleshooting missing, dim, incorrect, or intermittent visual prompts and abnormal status indicators caused by batteries, accessories, contamination, damage, or internal failure.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting while the AED Plus is required for an active cardiac-arrest response. If a display, pictogram, or indicator fails during patient care: Continue CPR according to the facility’s emergency-response procedure. Obtain another verified AED or manual defibrillator immediately. Follow audible prompts only while transferring care to the replacement device. Do not rely on an AED whose readiness or rescue instructions cannot be visually confirmed. Expected outcome: Patient care no longer depends on an AED with uncertain visual-prompt or readiness-indicator operation. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the AED Plus has been removed from active service.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Exact Visual Failure
steps.instructions: Power on the AED in a safe, nonclinical area and determine whether the complaint involves: A blank or unreadable message display; Missing or incorrect rescue pictograms; Pictogram indicator lights that do not illuminate; A dim, flickering, or intermittent display; A Shock button light that does not illuminate when expected; A red “X,” blank condition, or abnormal indication in the status window; Visual prompts that do not correspond with the audible instructions. Record whether voice prompts and tones remain functional. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to the message display, rescue pictograms, individual lights, status indicator, or the entire visual interface.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the AED Exterior
steps.instructions: Turn the device off and inspect: The display window for cracks, clouding, scratches, or liquid intrusion; Rescue pictograms for physical damage or separation; The status-indicator window for obstruction or damage; The Shock button and surrounding light; The enclosure for impact damage, loose sections, or deformation; The device for contamination, residue, or evidence of improper cleaning. Clean only according to approved facility and manufacturer procedures. Do not allow liquid to enter the AED. Expected outcome: All visual areas are clean, unobstructed, and physically intact. If cleaning removes an obstruction and the visual indicators operate normally during testing, document the correction and stop.

steps.title: 4. Check the Status Indicator Before Power-On
steps.instructions: With the AED turned off, inspect the status window. A green check indicates that the AED passed its most recent self-test and is considered ready. A red “X,” warning beep, or failure to show the expected ready indication requires further evaluation. Expected outcome: The normal green readiness indication is visible with the device off. Do not return the AED to service solely because it powers on if its normal readiness status cannot be verified.

steps.title: 5. Confirm Battery Condition and Installation
steps.instructions: Inspect the installed batteries for: Correct battery type; Matching battery manufacturer and date code when required by facility policy; Expiration or service-life concerns; Leakage, corrosion, swelling, or damaged terminals; Incorrect orientation; Loose or incomplete installation. Remove and reinstall the battery set only when the AED is out of service. Ensure each battery is fully seated. After reinstalling batteries, allow the AED to complete its startup and self-test sequence. Expected outcome: The batteries are correctly installed, free from damage, and capable of supporting a complete self-test. If battery condition is questionable, replace the complete battery set with an approved, known-good set. Do not mix old and new batteries.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Electrode Connection
steps.instructions: Confirm that the electrode cable is fully connected to the AED and that the connector is not: Partially inserted; Loose; Contaminated; Bent or cracked; Pulled away from the cable; Connected to an opened, expired, or damaged electrode package. A red status indication or readiness warning may result from an electrode cable that is not correctly attached. Expected outcome: A compatible, serviceable electrode package is properly connected. If reseating or replacing the electrode package restores the green status indication and all visual prompts pass testing, document the correction and stop.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Controlled Power-On Test
steps.instructions: Power on the AED and observe the complete startup sequence without connecting it to a patient. Verify: The display activates and remains readable; Rescue pictograms or their indicator lights illuminate in the expected sequence; Audible instructions correspond with visual instructions; The Shock button light activates only during the appropriate test sequence; No section remains permanently dark, illuminated, distorted, or frozen; The device does not restart or shut down unexpectedly. The AED Plus uses coordinated audio and visual prompts to guide rescue actions and CPR performance. Expected outcome: Visual and audible prompts operate together without missing, incorrect, or intermittent indications. If the failure is reproduced, record the exact point in the sequence where it occurs.

steps.title: 8. Check for Environmental Effects
steps.instructions: Confirm the AED has not recently been exposed to: Temperature outside its approved storage range; Condensation following movement between hot and cold locations; Excessive moisture; Direct sunlight causing poor visibility; Dust or debris; Chemical cleaners that may damage display surfaces; Recent impact, vibration, or a drop. Move the AED to a clean, dry, temperature-controlled area and allow it to stabilize before retesting. Do not apply external heat. Expected outcome: Temporary environmental conditions are eliminated as the cause. The AED Plus is designed for demanding environments, but visible moisture, condensation, or impact damage still requires careful evaluation before reuse.

steps.title: 9. Compare With a Known-Good AED Plus When Available
steps.instructions: Use another verified AED Plus of the same configuration to compare: Status-window appearance; Display brightness and contrast; Startup pictogram sequence; Indicator-light timing; Audible and visual prompt coordination. Do not use a training unit as the sole performance reference unless its differences are clearly understood. Expected outcome: Normal model behavior is distinguished from a genuine display or indicator failure.

steps.title: 10. Complete the Approved Readiness or Functional Check
steps.instructions: Perform the facility-approved AED Plus readiness and functional inspection. Verify: Successful self-test; Green status indication after testing; Readable visual prompts; Correct pictogram sequence; Functional indicator lights; Proper audible prompts; Serviceable batteries and electrodes; No unresolved fault indication or warning beep. Do not perform an unauthorized shock-delivery test or connect the AED to a person. Use only approved test equipment and procedures when therapy verification is required. Expected outcome: The AED completes the approved test with all visual, audible, readiness, and accessory checks passing. If every test passes and the original complaint cannot be reproduced, document the inspection findings and follow facility policy for intermittent failures before returning the device to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the AED Plus powered on, but the rescue pictograms did not illuminate and the status window displayed a red “X.”
CCR.Cause: Inspection found the CPR-D-padz connector partially seated, preventing the AED from completing its normal readiness check.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated the electrode connector, completed the approved startup and readiness test, verified all pictograms and indicator lights, and confirmed a green status check before returning the AED to service.

helpfulDetails: Green check, red “X,” or blank status window
Warning beep present while powered off

title: ZOLL AED Plus Defibrillator - Rescue Event Data Download or Infrared Transfer Failure
description: Troubleshooting failed rescue-data downloads caused by infrared alignment, IrDA hardware, computer settings, software access, device power, or communication-mode problems.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform rescue-data transfer troubleshooting while the AED Plus is assigned as the only available defibrillator for an active patient-care area. Before beginning: Remove the AED from active clinical service. Provide another verified AED for emergency coverage. Confirm that no patient is connected to the electrodes. Preserve the AED and associated rescue information according to facility post-event procedures. Expected outcome: Emergency response coverage remains available, and troubleshooting can be completed without affecting patient care. If the device is needed for another emergency, stop troubleshooting and return a verified replacement AED to service.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine which part of the transfer is unsuccessful: The computer does not detect the AED. The AED does not enter communications mode. The application remains waiting for a device. The transfer begins but stops or times out. No rescue event is found. Data transfers but cannot be opened. The wrong rescue event appears. Record any displayed computer message, audible AED prompt, progress-bar behavior, software name, and software version. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to AED communication, infrared hardware, software, data availability, or file access.

steps.title: 3. Verify the AED’s Basic Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect the AED Plus before attempting another transfer. Check for: A normal readiness indicator before removal from service. Adequate battery condition. Physical damage to the housing or infrared communication area. Contamination, labels, tape, or residue covering the infrared window. Evidence of liquid intrusion, impact, unusual heat, or odor. Clean only the exterior using approved methods. Do not insert tools into openings or disassemble the AED. Expected outcome: The AED is externally intact, adequately powered, and its infrared communication window is unobstructed. If the device displays a service condition or cannot power reliably, stop and send it for bench evaluation.

steps.title: 4. Confirm Compatible ZOLL Software Is Being Used
steps.instructions: Verify that the workstation is running a facility-approved ZOLL application that supports rescue-event data from the AED Plus. ZOLL currently lists RescueNet EventSummary as supporting AED Plus clinical-event data. Older environments may use ZOLL Data Retriever or another supported ZOLL data-management application. Confirm: The application opens without errors. The logged-in account has permission to run the software. The correct device type or infrared transfer option is selected. The workstation meets the software’s compatibility requirements. Endpoint security has not blocked the application or its device driver. Expected outcome: The approved ZOLL application is operating normally and is configured for an AED Plus infrared transfer. If the software will not launch or is not approved for the workstation, correct the computer issue before troubleshooting the AED further.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Infrared Adapter
steps.instructions: Inspect the workstation’s IrDA adapter or integrated infrared port. Confirm: The adapter is securely connected. Windows recognizes the adapter without a warning symbol. The correct driver is installed. The infrared port is enabled. No USB extension, docking station, or hub is causing an intermittent connection. The adapter is not being used by another application. Disconnect and reconnect the adapter. When practical, connect it directly to another known-good USB port and allow the operating system to recognize it fully. Expected outcome: The infrared adapter appears normally in the operating system and remains connected without errors. If the adapter is not recognized, test with a known-good compatible IrDA adapter before suspecting the AED. ZOLL states that an IrDA device is required for infrared communication with the AED Plus.

steps.title: 6. Align the Infrared Ports Correctly
steps.instructions: Position the AED Plus so its infrared window directly faces the workstation’s infrared port or external IrDA reader. Ensure: The infrared windows face each other. There is a clear line of sight. Neither device is moving. The distance is close enough for reliable communication. Bright sunlight or intense direct lighting is not striking the infrared windows. No equipment or cable blocks the signal path. Do not hold the AED by hand during the transfer. Place both devices on stable surfaces. Expected outcome: The infrared transmitter and receiver remain directly aligned throughout the communication attempt. ZOLL’s transfer instructions require the AED Plus infrared port to be aligned with the workstation’s infrared port or reader.

steps.title: 7. Start the Transfer in the Correct Sequence
steps.instructions: Using the approved data application: Select the infrared transfer method. Initiate the application’s upload or data-retrieval function. Press and hold the AED Plus On control. Continue holding it until the AED announces: “Non-rescue mode. Communications established.” Keep the AED and infrared reader aligned while the progress bar advances. ZOLL indicates that a transfer may take approximately 30 seconds to several minutes, depending on the record size. Expected outcome: The AED enters non-rescue communications mode, the software recognizes it, and transfer progress begins. If the AED begins normal rescue operation instead of communications mode, stop the attempt, confirm the button sequence, realign the ports, and retry once.

steps.title: 8. Allow the Transfer to Finish Without Interruption
steps.instructions: Once the upload begins: Do not move the AED or infrared adapter. Do not close the application. Do not remove the IrDA adapter. Do not allow the workstation to sleep or lock. Do not start another transfer simultaneously. Observe whether progress consistently stops at the same point. Expected outcome: The transfer completes and the rescue event appears in the application. If communication fails only when either device is moved, repeat the transfer with improved physical support and alignment.

steps.title: 9. Test the Computer Side With Known-Good Equipment
steps.instructions: When available, perform controlled substitution testing: Attempt to read another compatible ZOLL AED using the same workstation and IrDA adapter. Attempt to read the affected AED Plus using another approved workstation or known-good IrDA adapter. Interpret the results: Another AED also fails on the original workstation: suspect the adapter, driver, software, permissions, or computer configuration. The affected AED transfers successfully on another workstation: suspect the original computer environment. Other AEDs transfer successfully, but the affected AED Plus fails on multiple approved setups: suspect an AED communication or stored-data issue. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to the AED, infrared adapter, workstation, or software environment.

steps.title: 10. Confirm That Rescue Data Is Available
steps.instructions: Verify with the reporting department or clinical team that the AED Plus was actually activated during the reported event. Document: Approximate date and time of use. Whether the lid was opened or the device was powered on. Whether electrodes were connected to a patient. Whether rhythm analysis occurred. Whether CPR feedback or shock delivery occurred. Whether a later activation may have overwritten or replaced the expected record. Do not clear, delete, or overwrite rescue data while troubleshooting. Preserve any available files before changing software, reinstalling applications, or performing additional device tests. Expected outcome: The expected rescue event is confirmed as likely present, or the absence of a downloadable record is explained.

steps.title: 11. Verify the Downloaded Record
steps.instructions: After a successful transfer: Open the event using the approved ZOLL application. Confirm the AED serial number. Confirm the rescue date and approximate event time. Verify that ECG, event markers, CPR information, and shock information display when available. Save or export the record to the approved secure location. Follow facility procedures for releasing the information to the clinical quality or risk-management team. Expected outcome: The correct rescue event is readable, identifiable, and securely preserved. If the transfer completes but the file remains unreadable on more than one approved workstation, preserve the original data and escalate to ZOLL technical support or the responsible data-system administrator.

steps.title: 12. Restore and Verify AED Readiness
steps.instructions: After troubleshooting: Exit communications mode. Return the AED to its normal closed and ready condition. Verify the readiness indicator. Confirm the electrodes and accessories are correctly connected and stored. Confirm no service message or abnormal tone is present. Perform only the operational verification permitted by facility policy and manufacturer instructions. Return the AED to service only when readiness is confirmed. Expected outcome: The AED is either returned to service in a verified ready condition or clearly removed from service for repair.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that rescue-event data could not be downloaded from the ZOLL AED Plus through the infrared connection.
CCR.Cause: The workstation’s IrDA adapter was recognized intermittently and lost communication when the transfer began.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the defective IrDA adapter, realigned the AED infrared window, successfully downloaded and verified the rescue event, and confirmed the AED readiness indicator before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Unusual heat, smell, contamination, or damage
Data provided to the appropriate clinical department

title: ZOLL AED Plus Defibrillator - Unexpected Shutdown or Intermittent Power Loss
description: Troubleshooting unexpected shutdowns, restarts, or intermittent operation caused by depleted batteries, improper installation, battery contacts, environmental exposure, or internal power faults.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting while the AED Plus is required for an active cardiac-arrest response. If the device shuts down or repeatedly loses power during patient care: Continue CPR according to the emergency-response protocol. Obtain another verified AED or manual defibrillator immediately. Do not delay resuscitation while attempting repeated power cycles. Transfer defibrillation capability to the replacement device as soon as possible. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without relying on an AED with uncertain power stability. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the affected AED has been removed from active use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Power Failure
steps.instructions: In a controlled, nonclinical area, document whether the AED: Shuts down immediately after power-on; Operates briefly and then powers off; Restarts without operator input; Loses power when moved or handled; Shuts down during voice prompts, analysis, CPR feedback, or charging; Displays a red “X,” emits an off-state beep, or announces “Change batteries” or “Unit failed.” Do not repeatedly cycle a device that produces unusual heat, odor, smoke, or battery-compartment damage. Expected outcome: The exact shutdown pattern and associated indicators are identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Exterior and Battery Compartment
steps.instructions: Turn the AED off and inspect for: Cracked or impact-damaged housing; Evidence of liquid intrusion; A loose or damaged battery cover; Battery movement inside the compartment; Corrosion, contamination, or bent battery contacts; Unusual heat, odor, swelling, or residue; Evidence that the device was recently dropped or exposed to improper storage conditions. Do not disassemble the AED or attempt internal repair. ZOLL directs internal servicing to qualified repair personnel because of electrical hazards. Expected outcome: No external condition is found that could interrupt battery contact or make further testing unsafe. If significant damage, corrosion, heat, odor, or liquid intrusion is present, stop and remove the AED from service.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Battery Type and Installation
steps.instructions: The AED Plus uses 10 Duracell Coppertop CR123 batteries made in the USA. Confirm that: All 10 battery positions are populated. Every battery is the specified type. Batteries are installed in the correct orientation. No battery is loose, reversed, damaged, leaking, or from a different manufacturer. Old and new batteries have not been mixed. Batteries from different replacement dates have not been combined. ZOLL specifies replacing all 10 batteries together rather than replacing individual cells. Expected outcome: A complete, correctly installed, matched battery set is present. If installation was incorrect, correct it and proceed to the checkout test. If the issue resolves and the AED passes all readiness checks, stop.

steps.title: 5. Replace the Complete Battery Set When Battery Condition Is Uncertain
steps.instructions: Replace all 10 batteries when: The AED announces “Change batteries.” Battery age or replacement history is unknown. Batteries are mismatched. Any cell is damaged or leaking. Intermittent shutdown continues despite correct installation. The installed batteries have reached the applicable replacement interval. Remove all existing batteries before installing the new set. Insert 10 new specified batteries, following the compartment polarity markings. Do not mix the removed batteries with the new set. Press the battery-compartment reset button only after all 10 new batteries have been installed, as directed by ZOLL. Expected outcome: The AED has a complete, known-good battery source and initializes normally.

steps.title: 6. Confirm the Electrode Cable Connection
steps.instructions: Inspect the electrode connector and confirm that the compatible electrode cable is fully seated and undamaged. ZOLL instructs that the electrode cable be connected after battery installation and remain connected during normal readiness storage. A disconnected or improperly attached cable may produce a failed-readiness indication that could be mistaken for a power problem. Expected outcome: The electrode cable is securely connected, and no connector damage is visible. If reseating the connector corrects the warning and the AED passes checkout, stop.

steps.title: 7. Perform the Power-On Checkout
steps.instructions: Turn the AED on and observe the entire startup sequence. Confirm that: The AED remains powered continuously. Voice prompts are clear and uninterrupted. The device announces “Unit OK.” The correct adult or pediatric pad message is heard. The display and indicator lights remain stable. No “Change batteries,” “Unit failed,” or other fault prompt occurs. Do not use a patient or simulate therapy delivery during this check. Expected outcome: The AED completes startup without shutting down, restarting, or displaying a fault. If the unit shuts down again with a complete new battery set, remove it from service.

steps.title: 8. Perform the Manual Self-Test
steps.instructions: With the AED safely disconnected from patient use, press and hold the ON/OFF button for more than five seconds to initiate the manual test. ZOLL recommends this test when a self-test has failed. If the unit fails again, it should be removed from service. Observe for: Completion of the test; “Unit OK” confirmation; Battery-related prompts; Unexpected shutdown or restart; A red “X” in the status window; Beeping after the unit is turned off. Expected outcome: The AED completes the manual self-test without interruption. If it fails, shuts down, or restarts, stop troubleshooting and remove it from service.

steps.title: 9. Verify the Final Readiness Indicator
steps.instructions: Turn the AED off and wait approximately two minutes. Confirm: The green check symbol appears in the status-indicator window. No periodic beeping is heard. The unit remains off without restarting. Gentle normal handling does not cause the indicator to change or the unit to power-cycle. ZOLL’s checkout procedure requires the green check to appear and no beeping to occur before the AED is placed into service. A red “X” or off-state beeping requires additional action and, if unresolved, removal from service. Expected outcome: The AED maintains a normal green readiness indication. If the green check remains stable after successful testing, return the unit to service according to facility policy.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the ZOLL AED Plus powered on normally but shut down intermittently during the startup voice prompts.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found a mixed and partially depleted set of CR123 batteries; the AED failed to maintain power until all 10 batteries were replaced together.
CCR.Resolution: Installed 10 new approved Duracell Coppertop CR123 batteries, completed the manual self-test and startup checkout, verified the green readiness check with no beeping, and returned the AED to service.

helpfulDetails: Battery manufacturer, type, quantity, and replacement date
Whether all 10 batteries were replaced together
Red “X,” green check, or off-state beeping
Unusual heat, odor, corrosion, or liquid exposure

title: ZOLL X Series Advanced Defibrillator - 12-Lead ECG Acquisition or Transmission Failure
description: 12-lead ECG will not acquire, produces poor data, or cannot transmit because of electrodes, cables, signal quality, configuration, or connectivity.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Clinical Workflow
steps.instructions: If a 12-lead ECG is clinically urgent, obtain it using another verified ECG-capable device rather than delaying care while troubleshooting. Do not rely on an incomplete or artifact-heavy 12-lead for clinical decision-making. Expected outcome: The required diagnostic workflow continues while the device is evaluated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Whether Acquisition or Transmission Is Failing
steps.instructions: Determine whether the unit cannot obtain the 12-lead tracing, produces poor-quality leads, completes acquisition but will not save or send the record, or fails only at a specific transmission destination. Expected outcome: The issue is separated into signal acquisition, record handling, or communication.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Electrodes and Patient Preparation
steps.instructions: Verify all required electrodes are present, fresh, correctly positioned, and making good skin contact. Replace loose, dried, contaminated, or questionable electrodes and prepare the skin appropriately. Expected outcome: All required leads acquire stable signals. If acquisition succeeds after correcting electrodes, proceed to final verification.
